 When it comes to investing , you may know less than you think — and that overconfidence may be costly . Almost 2 out of every 3 investors rate their investment knowledge highly , and 42 % are comfortable making investment decisions , according to a recent report published by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority . [[Younger]] investors ages 18 to 34 were more likely to be confident than those in [[older]] age groups ( 35- to 54 - year - olds and those over age 55 ) . However , investors with more confidence also disproportionately answered [[more]] questions incorrectly on a financial quiz — suggesting that " many younger investors are not simply uninformed , but potentially misinformed , " according to the report . More from Personal Finance : 

 The best way to pay down high - interest debt 

 Where to keep cash amid high inflation and rising interest rates 

 3 changes to required withdrawals from 401(k ) plans and IRAs 

 Why your investment ' ego ' may be costly 

 This is n't to say that confidence is a bad thing . But " overconfidence bias " — the behavioral principle of overestimating one 's financial acumen — can have damaging results . " It should be no surprise that for the average investor , overconfidence can potentially be a pathway to [[poor]] portfolio performance , " Omar Aguilar , CEO and chief investment officer at Charles Schwab Asset Management , wrote on the subject . For example , this " ego - driven tendency " might trick your brain into thinking it 's possible to consistently beat the stock market with risky bets , Aguilar said . ( Hint : Statistics show it 's tough for the pros , so it 's bound to be hard for the average person , too . ) Beyond adding potentially unnecessary risk to a portfolio , overconfidence might introduce higher relative costs associated with the frequent buying and selling of assets , Aguilar said . 

 Social media contributes to overconfidence 

 Knowing how confident you should or should n't be is known as " calibration . " People are generally well - calibrated if they get frequent feedback on decisions , letting them know if they were directionally right or wrong , said Dan Egan , vice president of behavioral finance and investing at Betterment . The problem is that people do n't often get that feedback in financial settings , Egan said . " It 's very easy to have an impression of , ' Actually , I know a lot and have n't been proven wrong , ' " Egan said . " And we do n't go looking for it . " " We tend to protect our egos , " he added . " We want to think well of ourselves . " 

 watch now 

 Technology and social media have also made it easier for people to develop false impressions of their own knowledge and skill , Egan said . For example , investors can fall prey to " confirmation bias , " whereby they seek out evidence in [[social]] - media circles that confirms a previously held ( but potentially false ) belief about an investment . Of course , technology and the internet have also made it easier than ever to access information — though users must then discern whether that data source is accurate and reliable . And while younger investors may disproportionately overestimate their knowledge , the extent to which it 's doing them harm is unclear , Egan said . They might not have amassed [[much]] money so early in their careers , meaning a mistake may be less costly relative to seniors , who 've built up a sizable nest egg over their working lives and have more to lose . 

 When an investment is trendy , ' start watching yourself ' 

 Overconfidence bias tends to manifest most often with get - rich - [[quick]] type investment decisions , Egan said . " That 's when you need to start watching yourself , " he said . Take the meme - stock bonanza or the cryptocurrency rush in 2021 , for example . Millions of investors created brokerage accounts early in the year largely to capitalize on a runup in prices ; if they got in or sold at the wrong time , it could have cost them big bucks . 

 Similarly , overconfidence may lead rushed investors to accidentally buy the wrong stock , Egan said . For example , many investors bought the stock of Signal Advance last year following a tweet by Elon Musk , who told followers to " use Signal , " leading the stock to surge by over 400 % in a day . However , investors inadvertently bought the wrong stock — the Tesla and SpaceX CEO was referring to the encrypted messaging app Signal , whereas Signal Advance is a small component manufacturer .

text:
New York CNN Business — 

 As freight railroad workers look to Congress to provide them with paid sick days , millions of other American employees have no safety net if they fall ill . 

 The US does not have a national standard on paid sick leave , a rarity among industrialized nations . Roughly 1 in 5 civilian workers lack paid sick days , but the prevalence of the benefit varies widely by occupation and wage , according to federal data . Public sector workers , management and professional employees and higher - earning staffers are more [[likely]] to have access to paid sick days . 

 However , many others are not as fortunate . Roughly one - third of workers in service , construction , extraction and farming occupations do n’t have paid sick days . About half of part - time workers lack the benefit , as do [[more]] than 40 % of those in the lowest quarter of wage earners . 

 Overall , about 33 million workers have no paid sick days , according to Family Values @ Work Action , an advocacy organization . 

 The lack of paid sick leave hurts both workers and the economy , said Seth Harris , professor at Northeastern University and former top labor policy adviser to President Joe Biden . 

 Americans with disabilities or chronic conditions may be less [[likely]] to accept positions if they do n’t come with paid sick time , which creates [[structural]] barriers to employment , he said . And companies are n’t required to offer the benefit , forcing some people to come to work sick or face losing pay or their jobs . 

 “ The most disempowered workers – who are low - wage workers – do n’t have an opportunity to demand paid sick leave from their employers , ” he said . 

 Also , people who come to work when they are n’t well are more likely to spread their illness to others . This became a [[major]] problem during the early part of the Covid-19 pandemic among essential workers who lacked paid sick days . 

 “ It ’s a bigger issue of trying to take care of the [[entire]] workplace by making sure people know to stay home and that they have the flexibility to stay home if they are sick , ” said Emily Dickens , chief of staff at the Society for Human Resource Management , a trade association . 

 Railroad workers ’ battle 

 While the [[vast]] majority of union members have paid sick days , the freight railroad workers do not . Among other demands , they have been threatening to strike in order to get paid sick days that are not in the current contracts . 

 The railroads say that workers can use personal time if they need a sick day . But the unions argue that with current staffing levels and scheduling rules , it ’s [[difficult]] for workers to have personal days approved , and they are likely to be penalized or even fired if they call in sick anyway . 

 What benefits the rail unions obtain is now up to Congress , after the [[tentative]] deals – which lacked paid sick leave , but included [[lucrative]] pay increases – were rejected by the rank - and - file members of [[several]] unions . That led Biden on Monday to call for lawmakers to pass legislation averting a rail shutdown by officially adopting the tentative agreement approved by labor and management leaders in September . 

 Progressive lawmakers , however , demanded to add paid sick days to the contract . 

 “ At a time of record profits in the rail industry , it ’s [[unacceptable]] that rail workers have ZERO guaranteed paid sick days , ” Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders , an independent who caucuses with Democrats , tweeted Tuesday . “ It ’s my intention to block consideration of the rail legislation until a roll call vote occurs on guaranteeing 7 paid sick days to rail workers in America . ” 

 The House passed the tentative rail agreement on Wednesday , with 79 Republicans and most Democrats supporting it . Lawmakers also voted separately to add a provision that would give the workers seven paid sick days , which was backed by nearly all Democrats but only three Republicans . 

 It ’s [[unlikely]] that the provision will garner the votes needed in the Senate , which can pass the original rail agreement without the [[sick]] leave measure . At least 10 GOP senators would have to support providing paid sick days to the rail workers . 

 Government mandates 

 The Covid-19 pandemic focused renewed attention on the lack of paid sick days , as well as family and medical leave , in the US . 

 In one of its early relief bills in 2020 , Congress created temporary paid sick and family leave benefits for many workers who contracted or were exposed to Covid-19 , were caring for family members affected by the virus or had to care for their children after schools shut down . 

 However , the pandemic failed to convince Congress to pass legislation making the benefits more widely available to workers on a permanent basis . 

 Biden had called for a federally funded paid family and sick leave program for those who do n’t receive it at work as part of his hefty Build Back Better package in 2021 . The House passed a bill last year that included four weeks of paid family and sick leave , which would have cost $ 205.5 billion , according to the Congressional Budget Office . But the provision did n’t make it through the Senate . 

 Meanwhile , a growing number of states , cities and counties have been enacting paid sick leave laws in recent years . 

 Some 14 states and Washington , DC , have specific laws on paid sick time , while Maine and Nevada have more general paid time off laws that allow covered workers to use the benefit when they are ill , according to A Better Balance , an advocacy group . Also , 20 cities and counties have approved paid sick time laws . 

 Nearly 57 million workers are now covered by state or local paid sick time laws , according to an analysis by A Better Balance . 

 Advocates see the railroad workers ’ battle as an opportunity to renew interest in expanding the availability of paid sick leave . 

 “ Workers should be able to take for granted that they can stay home and take care of themselves if they ’re sick , ” said Mia Dell , deputy director of advocacy at the AFL - CIO , a federation of labor unions .

CNN — 

 For weeks , scientists have been watching a slew of Omicron descendants duke it out for dominance of Covid-19 transmission in the United States , with the BQs – BQ.1 and BQ.1.1 – seeming to edge out all the others to claim a slight lead . 

 The result has been a gradual rise in cases and hospitalizations that never seemed to reach the peaks of this summer ’s BA.5 wave and was certainly nothing like the tsunami of illness caused by the [[original]] Omicron strain a year ago . 

 But on Friday , the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention ’s Covid-19 variant dashboard revealed a new dark horse that could soon sweep the field : XBB.1.5 . 

 The CDC estimates that XBB.1.5 has more than doubled its share of the Covid-19 pie each week for the last four , rising from about 4 % to 41 % of new infections over the month of December . In the Northeast , the CDC estimates , XBB.1.5 is causing 75 % of new cases . 

 “ For a few months now , we have n’t seen a variant that ’s taken off at that speed , ” said Pavitra Roychoudhury , director of Covid-19 sequencing at the University of Washington School of Medicine ’s virology lab . 

 Virologists and epidemiologists say this Omicron sublineage has features that give it the potential to drive a new surge of Covid-19 cases in the US , although it ’s still unclear how large that wave will be and whether it could send many more people to the hospital . 

 For all the recent concern that a new Covid-19 threat could come from China ’s ongoing surge , experts point out that XBB.1.5 appears to have arisen in the United States . It was first detected in New York and Connecticut in [[late]] October , according to GISAID , a global effort to catalog and track variants of the coronavirus . 

 Trevor Bedford , a professor of computational biology at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle , said XBB.1.5 has a growth rate similar to that of its distant cousin BA.5 . 

 Bedford has pegged its effective [[reproductive]] number – the number of [[new]] infections expected to be caused by each infected person – at about 1.6 , roughly 40 % higher than its next closest competitor . 

 “ I expect it to drive increased circulation in the coming weeks , ” Bedford wrote in an email . That increase may not be reflected in case numbers , he pointed out , since more people are testing at home , and their cases may not be counted unless they seek medical care and get a lab test to confirm their results . “ So I ’d look to hospitalizations in the vulnerable age groups [ such as seniors ] as better indicator of wave , ” he wrote . 

 Slippery subvariants 

 XBB.1.5 is the product of recombination : Two descendants of BA.2 , the subvariant that drove a modest wave of cases in the US in April , swapped pieces of their genetic code , resulting in 14 new mutations to the virus ’ spike proteins compared with BA.2 , and a new sublineage , XBB . 

 XBB drove a wave of cases in Singapore this fall but never gained much ground in the US . Here , it had to compete against a slew of co - circulating variants that had each independently evolved some of the same mutations , making them more equally matched . 

 Still , scientists have been keeping a [[close]] eye on XBB and its spinoffs . 

 Dr. David Ho , professor of microbiology and immunology at Columbia University , recently tested viruses engineered to have the spikes of XBB and XBB.1 as well as BQ.1 and BQ 1.1 in his lab against antibodies from the blood of people who ’d been infected , who were vaccinated with the original and new [[bivalent]] vaccines , and who ’d been both infected and vaccinated . His team also tested 23 monoclonal antibody treatments against these new sublineages . 

 He found that XBB.1 was the slipperiest of them all . It was 63 times less likely to be neutralized by antibodies in the blood of infected and vaccinated people than BA.2 and 49 times less likely to be neutralized compared with BA.4 and BA.5 . 

 In terms of immune evasion , Ho says , these variants have shifted as far away from the antibodies we have made to use against them as the original Omicron variant was from the Covid-19 viruses that preceded it roughly a year ago . 

 He calls these levels of [[immune]] evasion “ alarming ” and said they could further compromise the efficacy of the Covid-19 vaccines . His findings were recently published in the journal Cell . 

 Ho said Monday that XBB.1.5 was the [[same]] story in terms of antibody evasion as XBB.1 , which means it has the potential to escape the protections of vaccinations and [[past]] infections . It ’s also [[resistant]] to all current antibody treatments , including Evusheld . 

 Another trick up its sleeve 

 In addition to being highly immune evasive , XBB.1.5 has an additional trick up its sleeve that seems to be helping to fuel its growth . It has a [[key]] mutation at site 486 , which allows it to bind more tightly to ACE2 , the doors the virus uses to enter our cells . 

 “ The mutation is clearly letting XBB.1.5 spread better , ” Jesse Bloom , a computational virologist at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center , wrote in an email . 

 This mutation was first flagged by Bloom , who studies the evolution of viruses and viral proteins , as one that could be important for viral fitness . It has been confirmed by Yunlong Cao at Peking University . 

 “ It ’s got a [[better]] ability to get into cells , ” Roychoudhury said , which means it ’s more infectious . 

 Still , experts say it ’s hard to know how much of XBB.1.5 ’s growth can be attributed to properties of the virus and how much simply to good timing . 

 Coming out of the holidays , during which time people were more likely to travel and socialize , gives any infection – whether it ’s the flu , Covid-19 or RSV – more room to run . 

 “ Most public health officials would have expected an increase in Covid-19 cases , even before we knew about XBB.1.5 . ” said Andrew Pekosz , a professor at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health who studies [[viral]] replication . “ So whether the increases in Covid cases that are occurring during the holidays are occurring because of the social interactions that people have had or whether they ’re specifically related to XBB.1.5 is still something that is n’t clear . Both of those things are probably contributing . ” 

 Most experts said that while they expect that XBB.1.5 has the potential to cause more illness , they do n’t expect those infections to necessarily be more [[severe]] . 

 Looking at the Northeast , where XBB.1.5 is thought to be causing the majority of infections , Michael Osterholm , who directs the University of Minnesota ’s Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy , sees reason for hope . 

 Osterholm notes that the updated boosters should provide some protection , even against this highly immune evasive strain . 

 Get CNN Health 's weekly newsletter Sign up here to get The Results Are In with Dr. Sanjay Gupta every Tuesday from the CNN Health team . 

 “ They still provide a level of immunity that may not prevent you from getting infected but may have a significant impact on whether or not you become seriously ill and die , ” he said . “ I mean , right now , the most recent data we have shows that for those who have the bivalent vaccine , they have a three - fold lower risk of dying than those who do n’t . ” 

 Americans have been slow to get the new boosters , however . According to CDC data , only 15 % of Americans who are eligible have had an updated booster . Among seniors – those age 65 and older – only about 1 in 3 have had an updated shot . 

 Experts also note that although antibody treatments wo n’t work against this sublineage , [[other]] antivirals , such as Paxlovid and remdesivir , should still be effective . 

 Rapid tests continue to work , as do masks , and ventilation and filtration of indoor air , so even as the virus continues to evolve , there are still good ways to protect yourself from getting Covid-19 . 

 “ It does n’t appear to be causing any more [[severe]] illness , and so I think that it ’s a very different situation circulating today than had it been a year ago , ” Osterholm said . “ There ’s so much more immunity in the population that I do n’t think that it ’s going to take off . ”

Shares of Cisco Systems rose more than 5 % on Tuesday after the company reported earnings and sales that beat Wall Street estimates and provided an upbeat outlook for fiscal 2023 . 

 Cisco reported adjusted earnings per share of 89 cents on revenue of $ 12.7 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter . Analysts polled by Refinitiv were expecting earnings of 77 cents per share on revenue of $ 12.5 billion . 

 The networking giant saw double - digit growth in its Security segment and a " return to growth " in the Applications segment . And while the company 's core switching and routing businesses were down slightly in the quarter , Chief Executive Officer Chuck Robbins said in a statement that he was encouraged by the strength in their other areas of focus . 

 Robbins also pointed to " record recurring revenue and software bookings ” as the company ’s “ total addressable market ” continues to expand . 

 Looking ahead , Cisco said it expects fiscal 2023 adjusted earnings per share to be in the range of $ 3.85 to $ 3.95 , compared to Refinitiv estimates of $ 3.74 . 

 “ We are transitioning to a growth mindset as we enter fiscal 2023 , ” Robbins said . “ We will focus on investing in key strategic priorities while continuing to drive operational discipline . ” 

 Analysts noted the positive tone of the company ’s guidance . 

 " We remain encouraged by the stickiness of the business model and prospect of margin expansion , which appears to be gaining more traction at Cisco , " said RBC analyst Robert Muller . 

 On a conference call with analysts following the earnings announcement , Robbins said the company will be increasing its focus on “ partner enablement , innovation and customer experience , ” as well as putting “ investment dollars behind applications , automation and analytics ” this coming year . 

 Cisco has been gaining traction in its transition to a software - as - a - service model , which allows it to expand its addressable market beyond traditional networking gear . 

 In the fiscal first quarter , Cisco said it expects to report revenue in the range of $ 12.5 billion to $ 12.7 billion . That compares to Refinitiv estimates of $ 12.5 billion . 

 Cisco 's shares rose more than 5 % in Tuesday trading to close at $ 54.72 per share . The stock has risen nearly 6 % so far this year .

Dear Abby : 

 I am in my 60s and single , with no children . I have had a successful career , but that part of my life is over . I have a few close friends , but I feel so alone and isolated . I know this is partially because of the pandemic and partly because of my age . I have lost the feeling of being part of something meaningful and valuable . 

 I miss the excitement of my former work and the feeling that I am contributing to the world . I want to find some purpose and meaning to my life . Do you have any advice on how I can find fulfillment without children or a job ? 

 Sincerely , 
 Lost and Alone 

 Dear Lost and Alone : 

 The pandemic has been especially difficult for people like you – those in their 60s , single and without children – as it has forced you to confront the loneliness that comes with age . I understand how disheartening it can be to feel isolated and no longer be part of something that used to give you joy . 

 But there are many ways to find purpose and meaning in your life , even without children or a job . One way is to become involved in your community , either through volunteering or through social events . Many organizations need volunteers to help with tasks ranging from tutoring , to delivering meals to the homebound , to being a friend to someone who is [[lonely]] . Not only will you make a difference in someone else 's life , you 'll feel like a valuable and contributing member of your community . 

 Another way to find fulfillment is to nurture your creative side . Paint , create art , write , or do anything that expresses your inner feelings . Or explore hobbies that interest you . Start a garden , learn a musical instrument , bake something new , or take a language class . 

 You may also want to explore ways to feel more connected to the world . Maybe you could become a mentor , join a book club or writing group , or travel ( when safe to do so ) . Social media can be a great way to make connections , as well , although it should never replace face - to - face relationships . 

 No matter what you decide , remember that your life has value and meaning . Age is just a number , and you are never too [[old]] to make a difference or find joy and satisfaction . 

 Best wishes , 
 Abby

Europe is moving closer to a single market that would limit the prices of natural gas for consumers , a move being championed by the European Commission ( EC ) as a way to protect consumers and bolster the energy transition . 

 The European Union 's executive body has put forward plans to create a [[regional]] pricing mechanism for natural gas , allowing individual countries to set their own regional price caps while still having access to a single European market . 

 The proposal , unveiled on Friday , is part of a larger effort by the EC to create an integrated European energy market and reduce the risk of market disruptions caused by the need to coordinate the different national markets . 

 The Commission believes that such a mechanism would ensure more efficient and [[transparent]] gas prices , reduce costs to consumers and ensure a more sustainable energy transition . 

 The proposal has been welcomed by many European countries , particularly those in Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean , who have long argued that they are at a disadvantage when it comes to access to [[natural]] gas at competitive prices . 

 Under the Commission 's plans , each EU member state would set a maximum price for natural gas at which it could be sold within the EU 's internal market . This would be based on data from the market and the broader European energy landscape . 

 The European Commission also wants to ensure that gas prices reflect the real cost of delivering energy , by including in the price the cost of energy transportation , storage and distribution . 

 The EC hopes that such an approach will help make gas prices fairer , simpler and more competitive across Europe and avoid the current fragmented market in which countries like Germany and France , who have access to cheaper [[domestic]] energy sources , can undercut their neighbours . 

 The proposed mechanism is part of a wider effort to move the European Union away from its reliance on fossil fuels , with the aim of becoming climate - neutral by 2050 . 

 The Commission also recently unveiled plans to strengthen the EU 's Emissions Trading System , which is designed to incentivise companies to reduce their carbon dioxide emissions by requiring them to buy allowances at auction . 

 The mechanism for natural gas price regulation is one of a number of initiatives that the Commission believes will help the EU reach its climate goals . 

 The move to introduce a natural gas price mechanism is expected to be formalised in the coming weeks , with the Commission hoping to put it in place by the end of the year . 

 The Commission has said it expects the mechanism to lead to an average reduction in energy prices of around 3 % to 5 % across the EU , depending on the market . 

 If agreed by the European Parliament and Council , the measure would come into force from 2022 . 

 Critics have argued that such a system could lead to higher costs for consumers , as the price ceiling could mean that companies pass the costs on to customers . 

 The Commission has sought to allay these fears , saying that the measures could potentially bring down energy bills by 5 % . 

 For the EU to move towards a more sustainable energy future , it is essential that it takes steps to ensure that consumers are adequately protected from [[sharp]] increases in energy prices . 

 The proposed mechanism is a step in the right direction and should be supported by the member states . A fairer , more integrated and affordable energy market in Europe could help bring down energy bills , promote competition and ensure [[secure]] access to energy sources , while also helping the EU reach its climate goals .

Jan 5 ( Reuters ) - Alex Mashinsky , a co - founder of bankrupt crypto lender Celsius Network who prosecutors allege bilked investors out of billions , is a serial entrepreneur who has portrayed himself as a modern - day Robin Hood . 

 Mashinsky , 57 , fraudulently promoted Celsius as a safe alternative to banks , while concealing that it was losing hundreds of millions of dollars in risky investments , according to a lawsuit filed on Thursday by New York Attorney General Letitia James . 

 The civil lawsuit seeks to ban Mashinsky from doing business in New York and have him pay damages , restitution and disgorgement . 

 James ' lawsuit is the latest black eye for the crypto sector , which has been rocked by accusations against FTX crypto exchange founder Sam Bankman - Fried . The former mogul , who has been accused of cheating investors and causing billions of dollars in losses , on Tuesday pleaded not guilty . 

 Mashinsky , a native of Ukraine whose family emigrated to Israel , decided to move to New York after he took a trip to the city in 1988 , he told a Forbes podcast . 

 " I looked around and I 'm like , I 'm never going back , " he said . 

 Since then , he has founded eight companies , including Arbinet , which went public in 2004 , and Transit Wireless , which provides Wi - Fi to the New York City subway . 

 Mashinsky claims to have created Voice over Internet Protocol ( VoIP ) , a precursor to ride - sharing app Uber , as well as an idea for a cryptocurrency that preceded bitcoin . 

 Mashinsky became involved in crypto in 2017 , when his venture fund Governing Dynamics brought on blockchain company MicroMoney as a strategic partner . He founded Celsius the same year . 

 In his teens , Mashinsky bought confiscated goods like hairdryers and VCRs from customs auctions at Israel 's Ben Gurion Airport and resold them for a profit , according to a 1999 article in the defunct tech publication Industry Standard . 

 Mashinsky had aspirations at the time to start a business for whole - body transplants : " Give an old person a new body - keep the head , keep the spine , and re - create the rest , " he said . 

 The executive served in the Israeli army from 1984 - 1987 , where he trained as a pilot and served in the Golani infantry units , according to his [[personal]] website . 

 Mashinsky has raised over $ 1.5 billion for various ventures that generated more than $ 3 billion when he and other investors cashed out of them , according to his website , which also says he holds more than 50 patents . 

 " The greatest risk is not taking one , " the home page reads . 

 In hundreds of interviews , blog posts and livestreams as the [[public]] face of Celsius , Mashinsky promised its customers that they would receive high returns if they deposited digital assets on his platform , with minimal risk , according to the New York AG 's lawsuit . 

 Neither Mashinsky nor his lawyer immediately responded to requests for comment on Thursday . 

 Celsius pledged investors would obtain returns of up to 17 % , among the highest in the industry . " We take it from the rich , " the lawsuit quoted Mashinsky as saying . 

 By early 2022 , it had amassed $ 20 billion in digital assets from investors . But the company struggled to generate enough revenue to pay the promised yields and moved into much riskier investments , according to the claim . 

 The company extended hundreds of millions of dollars in uncollateralized loans , and invested hundreds of millions more in unregulated decentralized finance platforms , the lawsuit said . 

 Mashinsky , who wore t - shirts with slogans such as " banks are not your friends , " continued to falsely represent to investors that Celsius was generating high yield through [[low]] - risk investments , according to the legal filing . 

 In an " Ask Mashinsky Anything " YouTube video on June 10 , the entrepreneur said " Celsius has billions in liquidity . " Two days later , it paused investor withdrawals " in order to stabilize liquidity and operations . " 

 Celsius filed for Chapter 11 protection from creditors last July 13 , listing a $ 1.19 billion deficit on its balance sheet . 

 Reporting by John McCrank in New York and Hannah Lang in Washington Editing by Lananh Nguyen and Matthew Lewis

 Amazon is shutting down its encrypted chat app Wickr Me , ending a four - year run of offering end - to - end encryption for everyday users . 

 The e - commerce giant said in a statement released on Tuesday that the Wickr Me app , which uses an encryption system developed by former National Security Agency cryptographer Will Ackerly , will no longer be available to download from app stores or accept new users . Existing users will be able to continue using Wickr Me , but the service wo n't receive any more updates . 

 The news is a blow to privacy advocates who had hoped that Wickr Me would help bring end - to - end encryption to a wider audience of [[everyday]] users . End - to - end encryption is a highly secure system that makes it virtually impossible for hackers or other third parties to access the contents of messages sent over the app . 

 The Wickr Me app , launched in May 2014 , promised an end - to - end encryption system that used complex algorithms to prevent snooping . The company said at the time that its system was so secure that it could be used for " higher - stakes conversations about business , family and [[other]] confidential matters . " 

 The Wickr Me app was popular among those who wanted to keep their messages private and was especially [[popular]] in the government , law enforcement , and corporate circles . But the app never really took off with everyday users , and Wickr struggled to monetize the platform . 

 In 2016 , Wickr announced a partnership with Amazon that allowed users to use the company 's encryption technology on Amazon 's messaging service , Amazon Chime . 

 However , Amazon has decided to put an end to Wickr Me and focus its efforts on its Amazon Chime service . In a statement , the company said : " At Amazon , we are committed to the security and privacy of our customers . We 've made the decision to close the Wickr Me app , so that we can focus our efforts on Amazon Chime , a secure business communication and collaboration service . " 

 The statement went on to say that Amazon Chime offers " [[unparalleled]] control " over communications including end - to - end encryption and [[key]] management capabilities . 

 It 's unclear why Amazon decided to shutter Wickr Me , but one possible explanation is that it was never able to get [[enough]] users to justify further development of the platform . 

 While the closure of Wickr Me is certainly a loss for privacy advocates , there are other services that offer similar levels of security . 

 Signal , a messaging service developed by Open Whisper Systems , is a popular end - to - end encrypted messaging app that is available for iOS , Android and Windows devices . WhatsApp , another popular messaging service , also recently added end - to - end encryption to its platform . 

 For those looking for an even higher level of encryption , the encrypted email service ProtonMail is a good option . ProtonMail offers strong encryption and privacy protections , as well as an easy - to - use interface . 

 Although Wickr Me is ending , Amazon 's decision to put its weight behind its Amazon Chime service and continue to develop end - to - end encryption is a [[positive]] sign for those who value their privacy . As more services offer robust encryption and privacy , it will become easier for everyday users to communicate securely .

For my book , " Raising an Entrepreneur , " I interviewed 70 parents who raised highly successful adults about how they helped their kids achieve their dreams . " Respectful parenting , sometimes called " wise parenting , " involves setting standards and [[strict]] rules ( e.g. , only spending money you earn ) while also being respectful of kids ' choices ( e.g. , letting them choose their own after school activities ) . 

 What is respectful parenting ? 

 When I tell people about the benefits of respectful parenting , they find it surprising and counterintuitive . Why would any parent let a young child make their own choices ? It 's much easier to step in before your kid does something that sounds like a bad idea , like wearing a Halloween costume to school in January or taking apart a radio . But respectful parents value individuality and do n't try to dictate what their kids are curious about or how they express themselves . Unlike popular parenting styles [[such]] as " permissive , " which overindulges children to avoid conflict , or " authoritarian , " where communication is one - way with little consideration of a child 's emotional needs , respectful parenting is about seeing children as independent , rational beings . VATICAN CITY — Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI , the [[shy]] [[German]] theologian who tried to reawaken Christianity in a secularized Europe but will forever be remembered as the first pontiff in 600 years to resign from the job , died Saturday . He was 95 . 

 Pope Francis will celebrate his funeral Mass in St. Peter ’s Square on Thursday , an unprecedented event in which a current pope will celebrate the funeral of a former one . 

 Benedict stunned the world on Feb. 11 , 2013 , when he announced , in his typical , soft - spoken Latin , that he no longer had the strength to run the 1.2 billion - strong Catholic Church that he had steered for eight years through scandal and indifference . 

 His dramatic decision paved the way for the conclave that elected Francis as his successor . The two popes then lived side - by - side in the Vatican gardens , an unprecedented arrangement that set the stage for future “ popes emeritus ” to do the same . 

 A statement from Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni on Saturday morning said that : “ With sorrow I inform you that Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI died today at 9:34 in the Mater Ecclesia Monastery in the Vatican . Further information will be released as soon as possible . ” 

 The Vatican said Benedict ’s remains would be on public display in St. Peter ’s Basilica starting Monday for the faithful to pay their final respects . Benedict ’s request was that his funeral would be celebrated solemnly but with “ simplicity , ” Bruni told reporters . 

 He added that Benedict , whose health had deteriorated over Christmas , had received the sacrament of the anointing of the sick on Wednesday , after his daily Mass , in the presence of his his longtime secretary and the consecrated women who tend to his household . 

 The former Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger had never wanted to be pope , planning at age 78 to spend his final years writing in the “ peace and quiet ” of his native Bavaria . 

 Instead , he was forced to follow the footsteps of the beloved St. John Paul II and run the church through the fallout of the clerical sex abuse scandal and then a second scandal that erupted when his own butler stole his personal papers and gave them to a journalist . 

 Being elected pope , he once said , felt like a “ guillotine ” had come down on him . 

 Nevertheless , he set about the job with a single - minded vision to rekindle the faith in a world that , he frequently lamented , seemed to think it could do without God . 

 “ In vast areas of the world today , there is a strange forgetfulness of God , ” he told 1 million young people gathered on a vast field for his first foreign trip as pope , to World Youth Day in Cologne , Germany , in 2005 . “ It seems as if everything would be just the same even without him . ” 

 With some decisive , often controversial moves , he tried to remind Europe of its Christian heritage . And he set the Catholic Church on a conservative , tradition - minded path that often alienated progressives . He relaxed the restrictions on celebrating the [[old]] Latin Mass and launched a crackdown on American nuns , insisting that the church stay true to its doctrine and traditions in the face of a changing world . It was a path that in many ways was reversed by his successor , Francis , whose mercy - over - morals priorities alienated the traditionalists who had been so indulged by Benedict . 

 Benedict ’s style could n’t have been more different from that of John Paul or Francis . No globe - trotting media darling or populist , Benedict was a teacher , theologian and academic to the core : quiet and pensive with a fierce mind . He spoke in paragraphs , not soundbites . He had a weakness for orange Fanta as well as his beloved library ; when he was elected pope , he had his [[entire]] study moved — as is — from his apartment just outside the Vatican walls into the Apostolic Palace . The books followed him to his retirement home . 

 “ In them are all my advisers , ” he said of his books in the 2010 book - length interview “ Light of the World . ” “ I know every nook and cranny , and everything has its history . ” 

 It was Benedict ’s devotion to history and tradition that endeared him to members of the traditionalist wing of the Catholic Church . For them , Benedict remained even in retirement a beacon of nostalgia for the orthodoxy and Latin Mass of their youth — and the pope they much preferred over Francis . 

 In time , this group of arch - conservatives , whose complaints were amplified by sympathetic [[U.S.-based]] conservative Catholic media , would become a [[key]] source of opposition to Francis who responded to what he said were threats of division by reimposing the restrictions on the old Latin Mass that Benedict had loosened . 

 Like his predecessor John Paul , Benedict made reaching out to Jews a hallmark of his papacy . His first official act as pope was a letter to Rome ’s Jewish community and he became the second pope in history , after John Paul , to enter a synagogue . 

 In his 2011 book , “ Jesus of Nazareth , ” Benedict made a sweeping exoneration of the Jewish people for the death of Christ , explaining biblically and theologically why there was no basis in Scripture for the argument that the Jewish people as a whole were responsible for Jesus ’ death . 

 “ It ’s very clear Benedict is a true friend of the Jewish people , ” said Rabbi David Rosen , who heads the interreligious relations office for the American Jewish Committee , at the time of Benedict ’s retirement . 

 Yet Benedict also offended some Jews who were incensed at his constant defense of and promotion toward sainthood of Pope Pius XII , the World War II - era pope accused by some of having failed to sufficiently denounce the Holocaust . And they harshly criticized Benedict when he removed the excommunication of a traditionalist [[British]] bishop who had denied the Holocaust . 

 Benedict ’s relations with the [[Muslim]] world were also a mixed bag . He riled Muslims with a speech in September 2006 — five years after the Sept. 11 attacks in the United States — in which he quoted a Byzantine emperor who characterized some of the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad as “ evil and inhuman , ” particularly his command to spread the faith “ by the sword . ” 

 A subsequent comment after the massacre of Christians in Egypt led the Al Azhar center in Cairo , the seat of Sunni Muslim learning , to suspend ties with the Vatican , which were only restored under Francis . 

 The Vatican under Benedict suffered notorious PR gaffes , and sometimes Benedict himself was to blame . He enraged the United Nations and several European governments in 2009 when , en route to Africa , he told reporters that the AIDS problem could n’t be resolved by distributing condoms . 

 “ On the contrary , it increases the problem , ” Benedict said . A year later , he issued a revision saying that if a male prostitute were to use a condom to avoid passing HIV to his partner , he might be taking a first step toward a more [[responsible]] sexuality . 

 But Benedict ’s legacy was irreversibly colored by the global eruption in 2010 of the sex abuse scandal , even though as a cardinal he was responsible for turning the Vatican around on the issue . 

 Documents revealed that the Vatican knew very well of the problem yet turned a blind eye for decades , at times rebuffing bishops who tried to do the right thing . 

 Benedict had firsthand knowledge of the scope of the problem , since his old office — the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith , which he had headed since 1982 — was responsible for dealing with abuse cases . 

 In fact , it was he who , before becoming pope , took the then - revolutionary decision in 2001 to assume responsibility for processing those cases after he realized bishops around the world were n’t punishing abusers but were just moving them from parish to parish where they could rape again . 

 And once he became pope , Benedict essentially reversed his beloved predecessor , John Paul , by taking action against the 20th century ’s most notorious pedophile priest , the Rev. Marcial Maciel . Benedict took over Maciel ’s Legionaries of Christ , a conservative religious order held up as a model of orthodoxy by John Paul , after it was revealed that Maciel sexually abused seminarians and fathered at least three children . 

 In retirement , Benedict was faulted by an independent report for his handling of four priests while he was bishop of Munich ; he denied any personal wrongdoing but apologized for any “ grievous faults . ” 

 Related Cardinal Blase Cupich is still keeping secrets on child sex abuse by order priests 

 As soon as the abuse scandal calmed down for Benedict , another one erupted . 

 In October 2012 , Benedict ’s former butler , Paolo Gabriele , was convicted of aggravated theft after Vatican police found a huge stash of papal documents in his apartment . Gabriele told Vatican investigators he gave the documents to [[Italian]] journalist Gianluigi Nuzzi because he thought the pope was n’t being informed of the “ evil and corruption ” in the Vatican and that exposing it publicly would put the church on the right track . 

 Once the “ Vatileaks ” scandal was resolved , including with a papal pardon of Gabriele , Benedict felt free to take the extraordinary decision that he had hinted at previously : He announced that he would resign rather than die in office as all his predecessors had done for almost six centuries . 

 “ After having repeatedly examined my conscience before God , I have come to the certainty that my strengths due to an advanced age are no longer suited ” to the demands of being the pope , he told cardinals . 

 He made his [[last]] public appearances in February 2013 and then boarded a helicopter to the papal summer retreat at Castel Gandolfo , to sit out the conclave in private . Benedict then largely kept to his word that he would live a life of prayer in retirement , emerging only occasionally from his converted monastery for special events and writing [[occasional]] book prefaces and messages . 

 Usually they were innocuous , but one 2020 book — in which Benedict defended the celibate priesthood at a time when Francis was considering an exception — sparked demands for future “ popes emeritus ” to keep quiet . 

 Despite his very different style and priorities , Francis frequently said that having Benedict in the Vatican was like having a “ wise grandfather ” living at home . 

 Benedict was often misunderstood : Nicknamed “ God ’s Rottweiler ” by the unsympathetic media , he was actually a very sweet and fiercely smart academic who devoted his life to serving the church he loved . 

 “ Thank you for having given us the luminous example of the simple and humble worker in the vineyard of the Lord , ” Benedict ’s longtime deputy , Cardinal Tarcisio Bertone , told him in one of his final public events as pope . 

 Benedict inherited the seemingly impossible task of following in the footsteps of John Paul when he was elected the 265th leader of the Church on April 19 , 2005 . He was the oldest pope elected in 275 years and the first German in nearly 1,000 years . 

 Born April 16 , 1927 , in Marktl Am Inn , in Bavaria , Benedict wrote in his memoirs of being enlisted in the Nazi youth movement against his will in 1941 , when he was 14 and membership was compulsory . He deserted the [[German]] army in April 1945 , the waning days of the war . 

 Benedict was ordained , along with his brother , Georg , in 1951 . After spending several years teaching theology in Germany , he was appointed bishop of Munich in 1977 and elevated to cardinal three months later by Pope Paul VI . 

 His brother Georg was a frequent visitor to the papal summer residence at Castel Gandolfo until he died in 2020 . His sister died years previously . His “ papal family ” consisted of Monsignor Georg Gaenswein , his longtime private secretary who was always by his side , another secretary and consecrated women who tended to the papal apartment .

Early 2023 has been a wild ride for weather across the world , with a range of extreme events including an unusual cold snap in much of the United States and a scorching heatwave in Europe . Scientists are pointing to two main causes for the wild weather : a stubborn La Niña event and manmade global warming . 

 La Niña is the cooler phase of an ocean - atmosphere phenomenon known as El Niño - Southern Oscillation , which is responsible for changing wind and rain patterns in many parts of the world . This winter , La Niña has been unusually strong and persistent , setting the stage for [[cold]] temperatures in some regions and warmer temperatures in others . 

 At the same time , manmade global warming is playing an increasingly [[significant]] role in extreme weather . This year , temperatures in much of Europe were significantly higher than usual , due to a phenomenon known as “ the fat finger of climate change . ” In this phenomenon , rising global temperatures make certain weather events more likely to occur and more intense when they do occur . 

 For instance , a study published earlier this year found that climate change was responsible for around 75 % of the extreme temperatures seen across Europe in the summer of 2019 . Another study showed that Europe ’s heatwave this winter was made at least five times more likely due to climate change . 

 It ’s not just Europe , however . A 2018 study found that climate change was responsible for at least 40 % of the severe drought in California in the previous year . In 2017 , Hurricane Harvey was made up to three times more likely due to climate change . And while this winter ’s [[cold]] snap was driven mainly by La Niña , climate change is likely playing a role in making the event more intense . 

 In short , La Niña is responsible for the wild weather we ’ve seen in some parts of the world this winter , but climate change is making these events more intense and more likely to occur . And until we address global warming , the extreme weather is likely to become an increasingly common occurrence .

As we move into the New Year , many of us will be looking at our health and making an effort to get it in check . For those with scleroderma and/or pulmonary arterial hypertension ( PAH ) , this can be an especially difficult challenge . The good news is that there are steps you can take to manage your condition and be proactive in controlling your health . 

 Scleroderma is a [[rare]] autoimmune condition that leads to hardening and tightening of the skin and [[connective]] tissues . It is a progressive condition that can cause a wide range of symptoms , including fatigue , joint pain , and difficulty breathing . For those with scleroderma , seeking prompt treatment from a healthcare provider is key to helping control symptoms and slow progression of the disease . 

 Similarly , PAH is a rare and serious condition that affects the heart and lungs . This disorder causes the walls of the [[pulmonary]] arteries to narrow , leading to difficulty breathing and other life - threatening symptoms . Treatment for PAH is often multi - faceted , and may include medication , lifestyle changes , and in some cases , surgery . It is important to work with a healthcare provider to determine the best course of action . 

 In addition to seeking prompt and appropriate medical care , there are also some things you can do to manage your scleroderma and/or PAH , and take control of your health . 

 First , it is important to have realistic expectations and understand the limitations of your condition . Working with your healthcare provider to set achievable goals and find ways to make everyday activities easier is key . For example , pacing yourself to conserve energy , using tools such as a cane or walker , and planning ahead are all ways to help manage the physical symptoms of your condition . 

 Another key element of managing scleroderma and PAH is staying active . Regular exercise can help maintain strength and flexibility , and can also help to manage fatigue . Research also shows that regular physical activity may help to improve symptoms of PAH . It is important to discuss an appropriate exercise plan with your healthcare provider , and focus on gentle activities that do not cause overexertion . 

 Staying up to date on medical research and treatments is also essential . For example , there have been significant advances in the diagnosis and treatment of scleroderma and PAH in recent years . Staying informed allows you to work with your healthcare provider to identify treatments that are most appropriate for you . 

 Finally , stress can worsen the symptoms of both scleroderma and PAH , so it is important to find ways to reduce stress . Mind - body therapies such as yoga and meditation can be helpful , as can talking to family and friends . Additionally , for those with scleroderma , support groups can be a great source of information and connection with others who are living with the condition . 

 By taking these steps , you can become an informed patient and take control of your health . Remember , you are your own best advocate , and only you know what will work best for you and your condition .

We 've all heard the same old advice on how to lose weight - eat less , move more , cut out [[unhealthy]] food , and so on . But what if these tried - and - true methods do n't work ? 

 Dieticians say that while these methods can help , they wo n't be enough to get to a healthy weight if you do n't look out for certain red flags . 

 " It 's really important that when you start a new diet or weight - loss program , you 're aware of any potential risks , " says nutritionist and dietician Cynthia Sass , a New York Times best - selling author . 

 To help you lose weight healthily and successfully , here are nine red flags that dieticians say you should be aware of before beginning a diet . 

 1 . A ' magic ' weight - loss food or diet 

 It 's not healthy to rely solely on one food , or even one type of food , to make up your entire diet . No single food is a miracle weight - loss cure , and while certain superfoods can help with weight loss , it 's important to remember that any food can still contribute to weight gain if you do n't watch your portions . 

 2 . Promises of quick weight loss 

 If a diet claims it can help you lose a large amount of weight quickly , beware . The reason for this is simple - it is n't [[healthy]] to lose too much too quickly . A safe rate of weight loss is 1 - 2 pounds per week . 

 3 . A plan that cuts out entire food groups 

 Healthy diets should be balanced , meaning they incorporate all major food groups and allow you to enjoy plenty of variety . Diets that forbid entire food groups , such as carbs or dairy , can lead to nutrient deficiencies , leaving you feeling tired and sluggish . 

 4 . A ' one - size - fits - all ' plan 

 No two bodies are the same , which means that no two people need the [[exact]] same diet plan . A plan that claims it 's suitable for everyone is likely not tailored to your individual needs , and could lead to nutrient deficiencies , weight gain , and other health issues . 

 5 . Extreme calorie restriction 

 Some diets restrict calories to as low as 800 or 1,000 per day . However , this is far too little for most people . Restricting calories too much can lead to nutrient deficiencies , dizziness , lightheadedness , and fatigue . 

 6 . Too much focus on the scale 

 Weighing yourself every day can set you up to become obsessed with the number on the scale , which can lead to unhealthy weight - loss behaviors . Instead , focus on other goals , like eating healthier , moving more , and building muscle . 

 7 . [[Unsustainable]] exercise 

 While exercise can help with weight loss , it 's important to remember that it 's just one part of a healthy lifestyle . If a diet plan suggests an hour of intense exercise every day , it 's likely not sustainable - or healthy - in the long run . 

 8 . Overly restrictive guidelines 

 Diets that forbid certain foods or snacks , or that do n't let you eat at certain times , are not realistic long - term plans . They can create unhealthy eating habits and lead to feelings of deprivation and guilt , which can contribute to weight gain . 

 9 . If it sounds too good to be true , it probably is 

 This is perhaps the most important red flag of all . If a diet promises results with no effort , or it requires very little in terms of food or lifestyle changes , it 's probably not an effective weight - loss plan . 

 By following these red flags and keeping them in mind , you can make sure you 're following a safe and healthy diet plan . With the right tools and knowledge , you can achieve your goals and maintain your weight for the long term .

The top - rated , non - alcoholic wine is made with organic Spanish grapes that are " fermented in stainless steel before being dealcoholized through vacuum distillation , " according to the company . 

 " Aromas are recovered and , after a [[short]] maceration , the wine is lightly carbonated and bottled , " Thomson & Scott said . It retails for $ 22 . 

 LaCroix 

 LaCroix 

 Personally , I 've realized much of the appeal of cracking open a beer or sipping a glass of rosé at the end of a long day is actually just the bubbles . If , like me , you 're looking for a bit of chilled effervescence , you ca n't go wrong with a simple , yet classic , seltzer or soda . Plus , it 's cheap — a 12 - pack typically costs around $ 5 . 

 If you 're feeling crafty you can even mix flavors and add a bit of fresh fruit to create your own mocktail . I 'm not that imaginative , so my go - to is typically a LaCroix ( tangerine flavor is my favorite ) .

 The Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards Credit Card is a great pick for students who spend a lot on dining , groceries , entertainment , and eligible streaming services . You 'll earn 3 % cash back in these categories with no limits , and 1 % cash back on all other purchases . 

 Until November 14 , 2024 , Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards Credit Card cardholders can automatically earn unlimited 10 % cash back on Uber and Uber Eats . In addition , through the same date , cardholders can also activate a complimentary Uber One membership , which comes with perks like $ 0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats orders , up to 5 % back on Uber rides , up to 10 % back with Uber Eats , and more . 

 You can earn a $ 50 cash bonus once you spend $ 100 on purchases within 3 months of account opening . That 's a low minimum spending requirement that [[most]] students can easily reach . 

 The Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards Credit Card also offers very good benefits for a no - annual - fee student card , including : 

 Price protection * * *

 Car rental coverage * * *

 [[Complimentary]] concierge services 

 Read our Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards card review for more info . 

 Best [[flat]] - rate cash back earning : Capital One Quicksilver Student Card 

 If you 're a student with no time to keep track of bonus categories and prefer straightforward cash back on all your purchases , the Capital One Quicksilver Student Cash Rewards Credit Card is a good choice . The welcome offer is $ 50 cash bonus once you spend $ 100 on purchases within 3 months of account opening . 

 As with the Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards Credit Card , the Capital One Quicksilver Student Cash Rewards Credit Card earns 10 % back with Uber and Uber Eats and offers a complimentary Uber One membership through November 14 , 2024 . 

 With this card , you can earn a lot of cash back quickly — all eligible purchases earn 1.5 % back , with no caps . It also comes with benefits you do n't often find on student credit cards , including :

 The Bank of America ® Customized Cash Rewards Credit Card for Students offers one of the most generous [[welcome]] bonuses of any student credit card . Like its grown - up equivalent ( the Bank of America ® Customized Cash Rewards Credit Card ) , new cardholders can earn a $ 200 cash rewards bonus after making $ 1,000 in purchases in the first 90 days from account opening . 

 The card 's other compelling feature is the ability to customize the category in which you earn the most rewards . You can choose to earn 3 % back on gas , online shopping , dining , travel , drugstores , or home improvement / furnishings on up to $ 2,500 in spending ( combined with the 2 % categories of groceries and wholesale clubs , then 1 % ) each quarter , and you can change your 3 % category selection once per month . 

 New cardholders receive a 0 % intro APR for your first 18 billing cycles for purchases , and for any balance transfers made within the [[first]] 60 days of opening your account ( then a 16.99 % - 26.99 % Variable APR ) . That 's handy if you 've got a lot of upfront expenses you need to pay off over time , like dorm decor or textbooks — but be sure you have a plan and means to pay off the balance before the intro 0 % APR period expires . 

 Best flat - rate cash back with an intro 0 % APR : Bank of America Unlimited Cash Rewards for Students 

 For those who prefer the simplicity of not having to keep track of bonus categories , the Bank of America ® Unlimited Cash Rewards Credit Card for Students is a strong choice . Along with a welcome bonus offer of $ 200 cash rewards bonus after making $ 1,000 in purchases in the first 90 days from account opening , this card earns 1.5 % cash back on all purchases with no caps . 

 New cardholders can also take advantage of an excellent 0 % intro APR for your first 18 billing cycles for purchases , and for any balance transfers made within the first 60 days of opening your account , followed by a 16.99 % - 26.99 % Variable APR . Whether you need to pay off your school supplies over time or are looking to splurge on a spring break trip , having a period of 0 % interest can save you money . 

 There 's no annual fee , but be aware the card adds foreign transaction fees , so it 's not a good choice for traveling outside the US . 

 Best for travelers : Bank of America Travel Rewards for Students 

 Students who love to travel — especially overseas — should have a look at the Bank of America ® Travel Rewards Credit Card for Students . Just like the non - student version ( Bank of America ® Travel Rewards credit card ) it comes with a welcome bonus of 25,000 online bonus points after spending $ 1,000 in purchases in the first 90 days from account opening ( redeemed as a $ 250 statement credit toward travel and dining purchases ) . Each point is worth 1 cent when you redeem for statement credits toward travel purchases , including airfare , hotels , rental cars , campgrounds , and even certain tourist attractions . 

 This is a good card if you do n't want to mess with complicated award charts or blackout dates , and its earning structure is simple — 1.5 points per dollar on all purchases , with no categories to keep track of . You 'll also get a 0 % intro APR for your [[first]] 18 billing cycles for purchases , and for any balance transfers made within the [[first]] 60 days of opening your account ( then a 16.99 % - 26.99 % Variable APR ) and no foreign transaction fees when you use the card on your adventures abroad . 

 Best for travel and purchase protection : Chase Freedom Student Card 

 The original , iconic Chase Freedom ® card is n't available to [[new]] applicants anymore , but its younger sibling — the Chase Freedom ® Student credit card — lives on . New cardholders can earn a $ 50 Bonus after [[first]] purchase made within the first 3 months from account opening , and 1 % cash back ( 1 point per dollar ) on all purchases . 

 Each year your account is in good standing , you 'll receive a $ 20 bonus ( 2,000 points ) , and you can earn a credit limit increase after making five monthly payments on time within 10 months from account opening ( when you meet credit criteria ) . 

 The Chase Freedom ® Student credit card has surprisingly good benefits for a no - annual - fee student card . When you use your card to pay for an eligible purchase , you 'll get the warranty extended by one year on manufacturer 's warranties of three years or [[less]] , and coverage against damage or theft on new items for up to 120 days ( up to $ 500 per claim and $ 50,000 per account ) . You also receive trip interruption or cancellation insurance when you pay with the card — up to $ 1,500 per person and $ 6,000 per trip for pre - paid , [[non]] - refundable travel ( like if you get sick and have to cancel or shorten your trip , or if it 's canceled due to severe weather ) . 

 You 'll also get other unexpected perks , including 5 % back on Lyft rides ( 5x points ) through March 2025 , and $ 10 per month in Gopuff credits through December 2023 . These perks are offered on the Chase Freedom Flex ℠ and Chase Freedom Unlimited ® , too . 

 Read our review of the Chase Freedom Student card to learn more . 

 Best for rotating bonus categories : Discover it Student Cash Back 

 The Discover it ® Student Cash Back can put a lot of cash in your pocket — if you 're willing to do a [[little]] work for it . When you activate the bonus , you 'll earn 5 % cash back in categories that rotate each quarter on up to $ 1,500 in combined spending ( then 1 % ) , and 1 % back on everything else . Discover 's 5 % cash - back categories often include popular merchants or types of purchases , like grocery stores , restaurants , and Amazon ( from January 1 to March 31 , 2023 , you can earn 5 % cash back at grocery stores , drug stores and select streaming services on up to $ 1,500 in purchases after enrollment , then 1 % ) . 

 While the card does n't offer a welcome bonus , Discover will match all the cash back you 've earned at the end of your first year . You 'll also receive a $ 50 statement credit if you refer a friend and they 're approved . 

 With the Discover it ® Student Cash Back , you 'll get a 0 % intro APR for 6 months on purchases on purchases ( then a 16.74 % - 25.74 % Variable ( as of 12/15/2022 ) APR ) , and if you accidentally slip up and make a late payment , there 's no fee the first time it happens ( afterward , it 's up to $ 41 ) . 

 To learn more , read our Discover it Student Cash Back card review . 

 Best rewards for gas and dining : Discover it Student Chrome 

 The Discover it ® Student chrome is almost identical to the Discover it ® Student Cash Back , with one [[key]] difference . Instead of offering 5 % rotating quarterly cash - back categories , you 'll earn 2 % cash back at gas stations and restaurants on up to $ 1,000 in combined spending each quarter ( then 1 % ) . All other purchases earn a [[flat]] 1 % cash back . 

 The spending cap on the 2 % categories is quite low ( $ 1,000 per quarter , or about $ 333 a month ) , but if you 're able to maximize this bonus , it 's worth an extra $ 20 per quarter . Students who do n't spend a lot in these categories or who want better rewards across the board will likely do better with a different card . 

 Learn more in our review of the Discover it Student Chrome card . 

 Best for [[international]] students : Deserve EDU Mastercard for Students 

 The Deserve ® EDU Mastercard for Students does n't offer remarkable rewards earning , but it 's unique in that you do n't absolutely need a Social Security Number to apply . That makes it an excellent pick for international students who would n't otherwise qualify for a US - based credit card . New cardholders can earn a free one year Amazon Prime Student subscription ( $ 59 value ) after spending $ 500 in the [[first]] three billing cycles on the card . 

 The card earns 1 % cash back on all purchases , but it comes with a number of valuable benefits , including cell phone protection when you use the card to pay your bill — you 'll be covered for damage or theft up to $ 600 with a $ 50 deductible , up to $ 1,000 per year . The Deserve ® EDU Mastercard for Students also offers rental car insurance and no foreign transaction fees . 

 [[Best]] rewards for on - time payments : Capital One Journey Student Rewards 

 Most credit cards penalize you if you make late payments , but the Journey Student Rewards from Capital One takes a slightly different approach . While the card still tacks on late payment fees ( up to $ 40 ) , it also incentivizes you to pay on time by offering bonus rewards for doing so . 

 Normally , you 'll earn 5 % cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel and then 1 % cash back on all other purchases , but you 'll get a .25 % bonus on all other purchases ( for a total of 1.25 % cash back ) each billing cycle if your account is not past due . 

 Capital One will also automatically review your account to see if you 're eligible for a credit limit increase , as soon as six months after you open the account . You can learn more in our Capital One Journey Student Credit Card review . 

 Best for building credit : [[Petal]] 2 Visa Credit Card 

 While not technically a student credit card , the Petal ® 2 " Cash Back , No Fees " Visa ® Credit Card ( card issued by WebBank ) is a good option for young adults with very limited or no credit history . The issuer does n't just rely on traditional credit scores for approval — it will also look at other factors , like banking history , income , and savings . What 's more , once you have the card , it 's reported to all three major credit bureaus , which can give your credit score a boost over the long term . 

 This is another card that gives cardholders an incentive to pay on time . Starting out , you 'll earn 1 % cash back on eligible purchases , but after making six on - time payments , you 'll earn 1.25 % back . After 12 months of paying on time , you 'll get a bump up to 1.5 % back . You 'll also have the opportunity to earn bonus cash back ( up to 10 % ) at select merchants . 

 Another bonus : The Petal ® 2 " Cash Back , No Fees " Visa ® Credit Card does n't charge any fees , including for foreign transactions or late payments . However , the card does n't offer balance transfers or cash advances like most others do . 

 Here 's our Petal 2 Visa card review with all the details . 

 How we chose the best student credit cards 

 We looked at [[several]] factors when evaluating the top student credit cards that are currently available to new applicants : 

 Simplicity — Does the card make it easy to redeem rewards , if any , and have a straightforward program ? Are there lots of complicated terms and conditions ? 

 — Does the card make it easy to redeem rewards , if any , and have a [[straightforward]] program ? Are there lots of complicated terms and conditions ? Earning potential — Does the card earn rewards , and do the bonus categories line up with typical student spending habits ? 

 — Does the card earn rewards , and do the bonus categories line up with typical student spending habits ? Welcome bonus — Student cards that offer a sign - up bonus or other incentives are appealing , especially for those on a tight budget who could use a rewards boost .

Options for different types of students — We included cards that appeal to all kinds of users , from products with a 0 % APR offer to travel points and cash - back credit cards . 

 Student credit cards frequently asked questions ( FAQ ) 

 Should college students have a credit card ? Chevron icon It indicates an expandable section or menu , or sometimes previous / next navigation options . Applying for your first credit card is an exciting milestone regardless of age , but young adults can find it hard to get approved with limited income and credit history . Some parents add their children as credit card authorized users while they 're still minors to get a head start on building credit , but this strategy is n't a good fit for everyone . Opening a student credit card is a [[great]] first step in building a solid credit history that will help you in years to come . As long as you use it responsibly , avoid carrying a balance , and make your payments on time , having a student credit card can help improve your credit score and make it easier to qualify for other types of credit , like loans and mortgages , in the future . However , if you do n't have the resources to make payments or are afraid you may overspend on a credit card , it 's best to wait until you 're in a better financial position . 

 Can I get a student credit card with no credit ? Chevron icon It indicates an [[expandable]] section or menu , or sometimes previous / [[next]] navigation options . Student credit cards are designed for those who have a limited or no credit history , so they 're typically easier to get approved for than regular credit cards . Other options include secured credit cards , which require a cash deposit , and starter credit cards , which are also geared to folks who are building or rebuilding their credit . 

 What is the best credit card for students ? Chevron icon It indicates an expandable section or menu , or sometimes previous / next navigation options . The best student credit card for you really depends on your spending habits and the types of rewards you like to earn . For example , if you spend a lot on dining , groceries , and entertainment , a card like the Capital One SavorOne Student Cash Rewards Credit Card would be a great fit because it offers bonus rewards in those categories . If you prefer a more hands - off approach , flat - rate rewards cards [[such]] as the Capital One Quicksilver Student Cash Rewards Credit Card or Bank of America ® Travel Rewards Credit Card for Students could be a better pick . You should also consider the card 's extra benefits , like no foreign transaction fees ( if you travel abroad a lot ) and purchase protections ( if you spend on big - ticket items ) before you decide on the [[right]] one for your wallet . 

 Can I get a student credit card in high school ? Chevron icon It indicates an expandable section or menu , or sometimes previous / next navigation options . You must be at least 18 years [[old]] to get your own credit card , regardless of whether you 're in high school or college . If you 're underage , you could still become an authorized user on a parent or guardian 's credit card until you 're old enough to apply for your own . 

 What happens to student credit cards when you graduate ? Chevron icon It indicates an expandable section or menu , or sometimes previous / next navigation options . After you graduate , your card issuer may convert your student credit card into an equivalent , [[regular]] credit card . For instance , Discover it ® Student Cash Back cardholders will have the Discover it ® Cash Back card instead , but still earn the same rewards . You might also have the opportunity to upgrade your student card to a regular version that earns better rewards , depending on your issuer and credit profile . Keep in mind there 's no harm in keeping a student credit card open after you graduate , especially if it does n't charge an annual fee . In fact , keeping no - annual - fee cards open for the long term can help improve your credit score by increasing the average length of your credit history .
