 Damar Hamlin 's collapse is the latest in a series of high - profile injuries highlighting the risks that come with playing football at the top level . 

 Here are some of the most notable injuries to rock the NFL that remind players of the risks that remain despite efforts to make the game safer . 

 Johnny Knox , December 2011 , fractured vertebrae 

 Chicago Bears wide receiver Johnny Knox after an injury in Chicago , Illinois , on December 18 , 2011 . Brian Cassella / Chicago Tribune / MCT / Getty images 

 Johnny Knox of the Chicago Bears suffered a career - ending injury in 2011 when a tackle bent his back the wrong way , leading to multiple vertebrae fractures . 

 Orthopedic injuries — accidents affecting the limbs — are the most common type of injuries in football , per the NFL physicians association . 

 Tua Tagovailoa , September 2022 , possible repeat concussion 

 A file photo of Tua Tagovailoa . Jeff Dean / AP Images 

 The Miami Dolphin 's Tua Tagovailoa 's high - profile concussion reopened a conversation about the risk for young players . 

 In spite of efforts made to reduce head injuries , notably after a groundbreaking hundred - million dollar settlement with former players , concussion is still a very real risk faced by NFL players . 

 In the preseason and regular season in 2022 , 187 concussions were reported , per the NFL website . 

 Tagovailoa passed out after hitting his head on the turf after a tackle in September . He self - reported temporary memory loss . 

 He had another violent knock to the head just four days earlier , which may have led to another undiagnosed concussion , an expert told Insider at the time . 

 If he had another head injury during the ongoing season , it could be career - ending , the expert said . 

 Rashad Johnson , September 2013 , severed finger 

 One of the most shocking examples of injury to limbs took place in 2013 , when Arizona Cardinals ' safety Rashad Johnson removed his glove after a tackle , only to find the tip of his middle finger had snapped off . 

 His finger had to be shaved down to the first knuckle . 

 Damar Hamlin , January 2023 , [[cardiac]] arrest 

 AP Photo / Matt Durisko 

 It is not clear what caused the Buffalo Bills player 's cardiac arrest during a game on Monday , January 2 . 

 But it is possible that the tackle from Tee Higgins of the Cincinnati Bengals triggered his condition , despite not immediately seeming exceptionally violent . 

 Experts say that a hard blow to the chest could trigger an undiagnosed heart issue . It 's also possible the tackle could have caused Commotio cordis , when a blow happens to hit at a very specific time in the heartbeat cycle and causes it to stop . 

 The NFL 's only in - game death : Chuck Hughes , October 1971 , heart attack 

 Chuck Hughes lies on the field at Tiger Stadium , October 24 , 1971 . Bettmann / Contributor / Getty Images 

 Hamlin is n't the only player to have collapsed on the field with a heart issue . In 1971 , Detroit Lions player Chuck Hughes had a fatal heart attack . 

 Hughes died of undiagnosed atherosclerotic coronary heart disease — a thickening and clogging of the arteries . He 's the only player to die during an NFL game . 

 Though there are not many examples of cardiac issues on the pitch , a 2019 study found that retired players may face an increased risk of having an irregular heartbeat called atrial fibrillation , which can lead to stroke , though [[more]] research would be necessary to confirm this trend . 

 Safeguarding efforts are underway 

 Las Vegas Raiders players wear a Guardian Cap during training camp on August 01 , 2022 in Henderson , Nevada . Ethan Miller / Getty Images 

 The NFL says it has been working hard to reduce the risk to players . Measures include improving the protective quality of the padding , deploying extensive [[medical]] teams at stadiums , and [[new]] game rules aimed at reducing risk . 

 In 2018 for instance , the league introduced a rule prohibiting players from ramming opponents head - on with their helmets , The New York Times reported . 

 The NFL is also discussing the rollout of Guardian Caps , a protective layer worn around the helmet designed to reduce concussive blows . These could reduce the risk of concussion for players by 10 to 20 % , and were tested in this year 's preseason . 

 In spite of these efforts , it 's not clear how much [[more]] can be done to protect players , former NFL player Donté Stallworth told CNN while talking about Hamlin 's condition . 

 " I do n't know if you can make the game any much [[safer]] , " he said . " This is a brutal sport . I think people forget that . "

text:
No country has a perfect COVID - vaccination rate , even this far into the pandemic , but America ’s record is particularly dismal . About a third of Americans — more than a hundred million people — have yet to get their initial shots . You can find anti - vaxxers in every corner of the country . But by far the single group of adults most likely to be unvaccinated is Republicans : 37 percent of Republicans are still unvaccinated or only partially vaccinated , compared with 9 percent of Democrats . Fourteen of the 15 states with the lowest vaccination rates voted for Donald Trump in 2020 . ( The [[other]] is Georgia . ) 

 We know that unvaccinated Americans are more likely to be Republican , that Republicans in positions of power led the movement against COVID vaccination , and that hundreds of thousands of unvaccinated Americans have died preventable deaths from the disease . The Republican Party is unquestionably complicit in the premature deaths of many of its own supporters , a phenomenon that may be without precedent in the history of both American democracy and virology . 

 Obviously , nothing about being a Republican makes someone inherently [[anti]] - vaccine . Many Republicans — in fact , most of them — have gotten their first two shots . But the wildly disproportionate presence of Republicans among the unvaccinated reveals an ugly and counterintuitive aspect of the GOP campaign against vaccination : At every turn , top figures in the party have directly endangered their own constituents . Trump disparaged vaccines while president , even after orchestrating Operation Warp Speed . Other politicians , such as Texas Governor Greg Abbott , made all COVID - vaccine mandates illegal in their state . More recently , Florida Governor Ron DeSantis called for a grand jury to investigate the safety of COVID vaccines . The [[right]] - wing media have leaned even harder into vaccine skepticism . On his prime - time Fox News show , Tucker Carlson has regularly questioned the safety of vaccines , inviting guests who have called for the shots to be “ withdrawn from the market . ” 

 Breaking down the cost of vaccine hesitancy would be simple if we could draw a causal relationship between Republican leaders ’ anti - vaccine messaging and the adoption of those ideas by Americans , and then from those ideas to deaths due to non - vaccination . Unfortunately , we do n’t have the data to do so . Individual vaccine skepticism can not be traced back to a single source , and even if it could , we do n’t know exactly who is unvaccinated and what their political affiliations are . 

 What we do have is a patchwork of estimations and correlations that , taken together , paint a blurry but nevertheless grim picture of how Republican leaders spread the vaccine hesitancy that has killed so many people . We know that as of April 2022 , about 318,000 people had died from COVID because they were unvaccinated , according to research from Brown University . And the close association between Republican vaccine hesitancy and [[higher]] death rates has been documented . One study estimated that by the fall of 2021 , vaccine uptake accounted for 10 percent of the total difference between Republican and Democratic deaths . But that estimate has changed — and even likely grown — over time . 

 Partisanship affected outcomes in the pandemic even before we had vaccines . A recent study found that from October 2020 to February 2021 , the death rate in Republican - leaning counties was up to three times higher than that of Democratic - leaning counties , likely because of differences in masking and social distancing . Even when vaccines came around , these differences continued , Mauricio Santillana , an epidemiology expert at Northeastern University and a co - author of the study , told me . Follow - up research published in The Lancet Regional Health — Americas in October looked at deaths from April 2021 to March 2022 and found a 26 percent higher death rate in areas where voters leaned Republican . “ There are subsequent and very serious [ partisan ] patterns with the Delta and Omicron waves , some of which can be explained by vaccination , ” Bill Hanage , a co - author of the paper and an epidemiologist at Harvard , told me in an email . 

 But to understand why Republicans have died at higher rates , you ca n’t look at vaccine status alone . Congressional districts controlled by a trifecta of Republican leaders — state governor , Senate , and House — had an 11 percent [[higher]] death rate , according to the Lancet study . A likely explanation , the authors write , could be that in the post - vaccine era , those leaders chose policies and conveyed [[public]] - health messages that made their constituents more likely to die . Although we still ca n’t say these decisions led to higher death rates , the association alone is [[jarring]] . 

 One of the most [[compelling]] studies comes from researchers at Yale , who published their findings as a working paper in November . They link political party and excess - death rate — the percent increase in deaths above pre - COVID levels — among those registered as either Democrats or Republicans , providing a more granular view . They chose to analyze data from Florida and Ohio from before and after vaccines were available . Looking at the period before the vaccines , researchers found a 1.6 - percentage - point difference in excess - death rate among Republicans and Democrats , with a higher rate among Republicans . But after vaccines became available , that gap widened dramatically to 10.4 percentage points , again with a higher Republican excess - death rate . “ When we compare individuals who are of the same age , who live in the same county in the same month of the [[pandemic]] , there are differences correlated with your political - party affiliation that emerge after vaccines are available , ” Jacob Wallace , an assistant professor of public health at Yale who co - authored the paper , told me . “ That ’s a statement we can confidently make based on the study and we could n’t before . ” 

 Even with this [[new]] research , it is difficult to determine just how many people died as a result of their political views . In the “ excess death ” study , researchers dealt only with rates of excess death , not [[actual]] death - toll numbers . Overall , excess deaths represent a small share of deaths . “ On the scale of national registration for both parties , ” Wallace said , “ we ’re talking about relatively small numbers and differences in deaths ” when you look at excess - death rates alone . 

 The absolute number of Republican deaths is less important than the fact that they happened needlessly . Vaccines could have saved lives . And yet , the party that describes itself as pro - life campaigned against them . Democrats are not without fault , though . The Biden administration ’s COVID blunders are no doubt to blame for some of the nation ’s deaths . But on the whole , [[Democratic]] leaders have mostly not promoted ideas or enforced policies around COVID that actively chip away at life expectancy . It is a tragedy that the Republican push against basic lifesaving science has cut lives short and continues to do so . The partisan divide in COVID deaths , Hanage said , is just “ another example of how the partisan politics of the U.S. has poisoned the well of [[public]] health . ” 

 What ’s most concerning about all of this is that partisan disparities in death rates were also [[apparent]] before COVID . People living in Republican jurisdictions have been at a health disadvantage for more than 20 years . From 2001 to 2019 , the death rate in Democratic counties decreased by 22 percent , according to a recent study ; in [[Republican]] counties , it declined by only 11 percent . In the same time period , the political gap in death rates increased sixfold . 

 Health outcomes have been diverging at the state level since the ’ 90s , Steven Woolf , an epidemiologist at Virginia Commonwealth University , told me . Woolf ’s work suggests that over the decades , state policy decisions on health issues such as Medicaid , gun legislation , tobacco taxes , and , indeed , vaccines have likely had a stronger impact on state health trajectories than other factors . COVID ’s high Republican death rates are not an isolated phenomenon but a continuation of this trend . As Republican - led states pushed back on lockdowns , the impact on population death rates was observed within weeks , Woolf said . 

 If the issue is indeed systemic , that does n’t bode well for the future . Other factors could explain the higher death rate in Republican - leaning places — more poverty , less education , worse socioeconomic conditions — though Woolf said he is n’t convinced that those factors are n’t related to bad state health policy too . In any case , the long - term decline of health in red states indicates that there is an ongoing problem at a high level in Republican - led places , and that something has gone awry . “ If you happen to live in certain states , your chances for living a long life are going to be much higher than if you ’re an American living in a different state , ” Woolf said . 

 Unfortunately , this trend shows no signs of breaking . The [[anti]] - [[science]] messaging that fuels such a divide is popular with [[Republican]] leaders because it plays so well with their constituents . Far - right crowds cheer for missed vaccine targets and jokes about executing scientific leaders . In an environment where partisanship trumps all — including trying to save people ’s lives — such messaging is both politically effective and morally abhorrent . The data , however imperfect , demand a reckoning with the consequences of such a strategy not only during the pandemic but over the past few decades , and in the years to come . But to acknowledge how many Republicans did n’t have to die would mean giving credence to scientific and medical expertise . So long as America remains locked in a poisonous partisan battle in which science is wrongly dismissed as being associated with the left , the death toll will only rise .

It ’s been a tumultuous year for the stock market — from the coronavirus pandemic to the roller coaster ride of technological stocks , traders have been kept on their toes . And now , the Securities and Exchange Commission ( SEC ) is gearing up to make changes to how the stock market operates . 

 SEC Chairman Gary Gensler is moving forward with his mission to update the decades - [[old]] system of regulations to better serve the investing public . At the same time , Gensler has taken a hard stance against Wall Street abuses , including insider trading and market manipulation . 

 In a speech on Tuesday , Gensler laid out his plans to reform the stock market , focusing on four key areas . First , he wants to update the rules governing the trading of stocks and other assets . He also proposed making sure that market makers have the resources and expertise to execute trades quickly and accurately . Additionally , Gensler wants to modernize the data reporting system so that investors have the latest information about their investments . Finally , he called for stronger enforcement against fraudulent and manipulative behavior in the markets . 

 Gensler said the SEC would look to apply some of the regulations from the bond market , which are stricter and better enforced than those in the stock market . He also proposed increasing the amount of information that market makers are required to provide about the trades they make . 

 The SEC also wants to update the rules for short selling , a practice in which traders bet on a stock ’s price going down . Gensler said that current regulations do not adequately protect against manipulation or market volatility . 

 In addition , Gensler called for the SEC to address the issue of market concentration , which can give some investors an advantage over others . He said that the SEC should take steps to ensure that the markets are open and fair to all investors . 

 Finally , Gensler also proposed taking a closer look at high - frequency trading , which uses powerful computers and algorithms to execute trades at speeds much faster than humans can . Gensler said that while high - frequency trading has helped to make markets more [[efficient]] , it can also result in market disruptions . He said the SEC would consider creating new regulations to protect the markets from disruptive behavior . 

 Gensler ’s speech follows a string of announcements from the SEC this year , all of which are aimed at modernizing how the stock market operates . In April , the agency proposed changes to how mutual funds and other investment products are managed . In June , the SEC imposed new regulations on hedge funds , private equity firms and other alternative investments . And most recently , Gensler proposed changes to how initial [[public]] offerings are conducted . 

 The stock market has seen some wild swings over the past few months , with the Nasdaq Composite index up 22.9 % this year and the S&P 500 index up 11.1 % . Gensler ’s plans to update the rules of the markets and make sure that investors are better protected could go a [[long]] way in restoring investor confidence . Only time will tell , but it looks like the SEC is determined to make the stock market a safer and fairer place for everyone involved .

It was like ‘ ‘ trying to pull nails out of an old log , ’’ Blackhawks coach Luke Richardson said , but wing Patrick Kane finally admitted he needed to sit out Friday . 

 Still hobbled by a lower - body injury suffered when he was hit by the Sharks ’ Evgeny Svechnikov last weekend , Kane ’s absence was his first because of injury since 2015 . 

 But even without the services of their leading scorer , the Hawks put together one of their [[best]] efforts of the season in a 2 - 0 victory against the Coyotes . 

 ‘ ‘ It was a complete game , ’’ Richardson said . ‘ ‘ Right from start to finish , I was pretty happy with the performance . ’’ 

 Defenseman Jake McCabe scored the only [[non]] - empty - [[net]] goal of the game , the Hawks generated a season - best plus-10 scoring - chance differential and goalie Alex Stalock — who started for the fourth time in the last five games and has leaped past Petr Mrazek for the No . 1 role — stopped all 22 shots he faced . 

 It was the Hawks ’ first shutout in almost a full calendar year . The defensive corps cleanly executed a new tweak Richardson added to the system , but Stalock was — as often has been the case — the Hawks ’ best player . 

 ‘ ‘ We boxed out , I got to see the first shot — which is always a bonus — and [ we ] cleared out any rebounds that were there the rest of the way , ’’ Stalock said . ‘ ‘ It ’s the team , man . You ca n’t do that stuff on your own . [ If ] you ask any goalie , it ’s impossible to do on your own . The group was really good tonight . ’’ 

 The Hawks deployed top prospect Lukas Reichel alongside Max Domi and Philipp Kurashev on their [[first]] line , and Reichel looked noticeably more confident and assertive than in his previous 12 NHL appearances . 

 But fortunately for Kane — as well as the Hawks ’ interests in potentially trading him at some point — his injury does n’t sound major . He participated in the morning skate Friday . 

 ‘ ‘ I do n’t think it ’s anything extremely long - term or anything like that , ’’ Kane said . ‘ ‘ So [ I ’ll ] just take it day by day here . 

 ‘ ‘ To be [[honest]] with you , I probably could play . But it ’s just [ in ] certain situations , it ’s kind of lingering pain . It is what it is right now . But I think I should be through it here quick enough . ’’ 

 The Hawks ’ [[next]] game is at home Sunday against the Flames ; Kane ’s status for that game is [[iffy]] . If he sits it out , he ’ll have a three - day break to rest and heal before the Avalanche come to town . 

 World juniors recap 

 Four Hawks prospects — forward Colton Dach and defensemen Kevin Korchinski , Nolan Allan and Ethan Del Mastro — got gold medals after Canada defeated Czechia to conclude the 2023 world junior championships Thursday . 

 Dach suffered a scary - looking shoulder injury earlier in the tournament but was on the ice in high spirits for the postgame celebration . He finished with two points in four games . Korchinski had four points , Del Mastro three and Allan two in seven games each , although Korchinski was n’t as dominant as hoped . 

 The Hawks ’ other tournament participant was Swedish forward Victor Stjernborg , a fourth - round pick in 2021 , who recorded two points in seven games , including a massive late goal to lift Sweden past Finland in the quarterfinals . 

 Among the three [[top]] 2023 draft - eligible prospects — Connor Bedard , Adam Fantilli and Leo Carlsson — whom the Hawks surely were watching closely , Bedard cemented his status as the slam - dunk No . 1 overall pick . He tore up the tournament and stuffed highlight reels worldwide with a historic 23 points in seven games for Canada .

 The set , dubbed “ TIE Fighter : 20th Anniversary Edition , ” is an updated version of the classic TIE fighter set that was released way back in 2003 , when the first Star Wars prequel was in theaters . 

 The new set is an exact replica of the original TIE fighter , but with some [[modern]] updates . The [[first]] thing that stands out is the fact that this set is twice the size of the original . It measures almost 17 inches in width and 11 inches in height , so it ’s definitely a great display piece for any Star Wars fan . 

 In addition to the size difference , the updated TIE fighter also features a [[few]] modern features . There are two all - new red Imperial crest badges and a new mini - figure that you can control from the cockpit . The mini - figure , which is a new version of Darth Vader , is compatible with all LEGO Star Wars sets . 

 The new TIE Fighter : 20th Anniversary Edition set also includes a special black box with a unique digital [[serial]] number that grants access to exclusive content and exclusive in - game rewards in LEGO Star Wars : The Skywalker Saga .

 Fans who purchase the TIE Fighter : 20th Anniversary Edition set can look forward to exploring the world of Star Wars even more . The set contains all the pieces needed to build the fighter , plus mini - figures of Darth Vader , Anakin Skywalker , and C-3PO . 

 Overall , this new set is an exciting addition to the LEGO Star Wars universe . Fans have been waiting a long time for a modern update to the iconic TIE fighter , and this set is sure to be a hit .  No word yet on when the set will be available to purchase , but it ’s likely that it will be released in the near future . So keep an eye out if you ’re a Star Wars fan , because this set is sure to be a must - have item for any LEGO enthusiast .

Bankman - Fried had been implicated in an SEC investigation surrounding illegal trading practices that had allegedly earned him more than $ 1 billion in profits . 

 The news came as a shock to many , especially considering that just minutes before , Bankman - Fried had been spotted in the American Airlines lounge at JFK , enjoying a glass of champagne and some snacks . 

 Details surrounding Bankman - Fried 's arrest began to emerge over the next few days . According to witnesses , authorities arrived at JFK shortly after Bankman - Fried had finished his snack and champagne in the lounge . He was quietly taken into custody without incident , despite reportedly being " chill " and calm in the lounge . 

 It soon became clear why Bankman - Fried had been [[calm]] in the face of imminent arrest . Prior to his detainment , he had arranged a business class ticket on an American Airlines flight to London , where he was planning to meet with his parents before returning to the United States to stand trial . 

 Over the course of the next few days , more details of the alleged insider trading case against Bankman - Fried began to emerge . According to the SEC , Bankman - Fried had been involved in a complicated series of trades that had allowed him to reap over $ 1 billion in profits . 

 At the [[same]] time , other reports suggested that Bankman - Fried had been tipped off about upcoming acquisitions and market changes that would allow him to capitalize on them before they became public information . 

 The news of Bankman - Fried 's arrest sent shockwaves through the cryptocurrency world , as many had come to respect the founder of FTX as a respected and successful investor . 

 As of now , Bankman - Fried is still awaiting trial . While the details of the charges against him remain [[unclear]] , it appears that the SEC is hoping to make an example out of him . 

 In the meantime , the story of Bankman - Fried 's " chill " attitude in the face of arrest remains a [[fascinating]] one . While he was seemingly calm in the face of his own impending charges , the future of FTX and the cryptocurrency world as a whole still hang in the balance .

The firm initiated coverage of the tech bellwether with a buy rating and $ 270 price target , viewing its investment in the research company , which operates ChatGPT , as a potential short - term catalyst for shares that help support its premium valuation . " [[Longer]] - term , we believe incorporating ChatGPT capabilities into Bing may provide Microsoft with a once - a - decade opportunity to unseat Google 's Search dominance , " wrote analyst Gil Luria in a note to clients Wednesday . ChatGPT is an artificial intelligence chatbot able to answer questions and write essays . It went viral after its debut in late last year , raising concerns over whether the platform could disrupt Google 's bread - and - butter search business . The " value - creation " opportunities ChatGPT offers both Microsoft 's Bing and Azure products have yet to materialize in the company 's current share price , but should support advertising , cloud and search growth , Luria said . " Furthermore , we believe Google will need to face a major case of innovator 's dilemma in deciding to incorporate generative AI into Search , thus significantly disrupting its current ad selling model , " he wrote . Microsoft suffered in 2022 along with [[other]] technology stocks , tumbling nearly 29 % as growth stocks took a hit in a rising rate environment . Looking ahead , Luria expects the company 's market dominancy and endurance to help the company weather [[further]] uncertainty ahead . The firm 's $ 270 price target implies nearly 18 % upside from Wednesday 's close . " Our price target represents a 50 % premium to the market multiple , at the high end of the 5 - year historical range , based on our expectation that the upside from OpenAI is not yet reflected in expectations , " he said . — CNBC 's Michael Bloom contributed reporting

Since the beginning of his administration , President Joe Biden has made it clear that he will take a proactive approach to climate change . That commitment has been reinforced with a series of actions taken by the new administration , from rejoining the Paris Climate Agreement to naming a special White House Climate Czar . Now , the Biden administration has taken another step toward reshaping the way people save for retirement by rolling back Trump - era rules on environmental , social and governance ( ESG ) investing for 401(k ) plans . 

 The change was revealed Thursday in an opinion letter from the Department of Labor ( DOL ) that had been requested by a coalition of asset management and consumer groups . The letter alters an earlier Trump - era decision that required 401(k ) plans to provide evidence of their ESG investments ' " [[financial]] " quality — meaning that they were not allowed to invest in companies that did not meet certain financial criteria . 

 The Biden administration 's opinion letter states that " ESG investments can provide a financial benefit that is comparable to that of non - ESG investments , and hence the Department will not take enforcement action if [ 401(k ) plans ] make investments based on ESG considerations alone , without considering financial factors , provided such investments would satisfy their fiduciary duties . " 

 ESG investing is focused on sustainable investing , favoring investments that have both a [[financial]] return as well as an environmental , social , or corporate governance benefit . It has been gaining in popularity , as [[more]] investors have become increasingly conscious of the environmental , social , and governance risks faced by companies . The Biden administration 's opinion letter removes the financial burden of proof from ESG investments . 

 " The Biden administration 's action should make it easier for 401(k ) plans to invest in ESG funds , enabling investors to select options that prioritize their own values , " said Maggie O'Kane , a senior fellow at the National Consumer Law Center . " This is a major step in the right direction and could help accelerate the growth of ESG investing in the U.S. and set the stage for other policy decisions to come . " 

 The Biden administration 's opinion letter , however , does not alter the obligation for 401(k ) plans to act in the best interests of their participants when investing in ESG funds . It does , however , provide a pathway for plans to select investments based on ESG criteria without first having to meet a [[financial]] threshold . 

 That is a crucial departure from the Trump administration 's stance , which had imposed a financial hurdle that was seen by some as a barrier to ESG investing . 

 The Biden administration 's action is the latest in a string of [[executive]] orders , memos , and other policy changes geared toward addressing climate change . Last week , Biden named Gina McCarthy , who previously led the Environmental Protection Agency under President Obama , to a newly created role as White House Climate Czar . 

 In his [[first]] three months in office , Biden has also implemented more than 200 executive actions aimed at combating climate change , from tightening fuel economy standards to setting a goal of conserving at least 30 % of public lands and waters by 2030 . 

 The Biden administration 's move to loosen restrictions on ESG investing signals the importance of this rapidly growing industry , as well as the White House 's commitment to tackling climate change . 

 " The Department of Labor 's opinion letter is an important signal to retirement plan sponsors and their advisers that environmental , social , and governance considerations are legitimate factors that can be taken into account when selecting investments for retirement plan portfolios , " said Tim Keating , CEO of Keating Investment Management , in a statement . " This is an important step forward for the retirement plan industry and for ESG investing in general . " 

 With the Biden administration 's move , plans will no longer be hamstrung by the Trump - era rules . That could provide a [[major]] boost to the ESG industry , particularly as investors increasingly prioritize their values when saving for retirement .

 It 's been almost 20 years since the iconic Indie Rock band Pavement first released their debut album and yet their influence still resonates throughout the music landscape . From their alternative rock style and lyrics that skewered society to their intense and infectious live shows , Pavement has been an influence for [[countless]] bands , fans and listeners . As the years have passed , the band 's influence has grown , with new generations of fans discovering Pavement and the timelessness of their music .

 The exact impact that consuming microplastics has on human health is still not clear .  Turkey 's current account deficit widened slightly to $ 4.1 billion in November from $ 3.9 billion in the same period last year , data from the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey ( CBRT ) showed on Monday . 

 The current account deficit for the whole of 2022 was seen at $ 48 billion , down from $ 50.1 billion in 2021 . The deficit reached a peak of $ 72.2 billion in 2020 . 

 The November current account deficit was in line with market expectations . Analysts had expected the deficit to remain flat at around $ 4 billion . The CBRT had forecast a deficit of around $ 5 billion for November . 

 The trade balance also narrowed in November , to a surplus of $ 898 million from a surplus of $ 2.2 billion in November 2020 . The surplus came after nine months of deficits , with the 2021 total amounting to a deficit of $ 5.1 billion , the CBRT data showed . 

 Turkey 's current account balance was supported by higher receipts from the services sector , with income from tourism remaining healthy . Receipts from the services sector , including tourism and transportation , rose to $ 7.6 billion in November , compared with $ 4.4 billion in the same period last year . 

 Meanwhile , exports fell on the year to $ 13.2 billion in November from $ 14.2 billion in the same month a year earlier . Imports also fell , to $ 12.3 billion from $ 13.9 billion . 

 The services sector has been the main driver of Turkey 's current account deficit over the past year , according to analysts . The tourism sector , however , is unlikely to return to pre - pandemic levels before 2022 , analysts said . 

 The CBRT has taken a number of measures to reduce the current account deficit , including increasing taxes on imports and implementing incentives for exports . The central bank has also introduced foreign exchange reserve requirements to reduce the foreign currency transactions of commercial banks . 

 Analysts said that Turkey 's current account deficit remains high and that further measures may be needed to reduce the gap . 

 " Despite the efforts taken by the CBRT , the current account deficit remained relatively high , " said Yigit Bulut , a strategist at Is Investment .

 Since the coronavirus pandemic took hold in March , the U.S. job market has seen an astonishing turn of events , with some 10 million jobs lost over the first half of 2020 alone . But since then , job gains have been muted , creating a lingering puzzle for the Fed to unravel . 

 " It 's been an incredibly frustrating puzzle for the Fed , " says Daniel Alpert , founder of Westwood Capital in New York . " It 's like putting together a giant jigsaw puzzle in the dark , and you do n't have the picture on the box to know what it should look like . " 

 The puzzle has been made more complicated by the fact that the jobless rate has been dropping — down to 6.7 percent in November , from its peak of 14.7 percent in April . This is far better than the 25 percent - plus unemployment rate that economists were projecting back in April , and it has kept Fed policymakers feeling cautiously optimistic . 

 But at the [[same]] time , job gains have been unimpressive . The U.S. economy has added an average of 228,000 jobs per month since May — far below the roughly 200,000 per month that is needed to keep up with population growth . 

 The Fed 's dilemma , then , is that the jobless rate is dropping but job creation has been weak . That disconnect has left some economists worried that the job market recovery is not as [[strong]] as the headline unemployment rate suggests . 

 " I think it 's safe to say that we are facing a ' missing jobs mystery , ' " says Michael Gapen , Chief U.S. economist at Barclays . 

 So what accounts for the disconnect between the unemployment rate and job gains ? One possibility is that long - term unemployed workers , who typically show up in the jobless rate , have had a hard time finding work due to structural and cyclical issues . 

 " It could be that more and more of these people are simply giving up looking , " Gapen says . " They know that there are still not a lot of job opportunities , so they do n't even bother to apply . " 

 That scenario would be particularly concerning for Fed policymakers , since it would suggest that the current jobless rate may not be a reliable indicator of the U.S. labor market 's health . 

 On top of that , the data is becoming increasingly mixed . In November , for instance , the headline unemployment rate dropped to 6.7 percent , but the number of jobs added that month was far below expectations .

 Alternatively , the Fed could decide to start raising rates , in an effort to prevent inflation from getting out of control . But that could put a damper on the economy , leading to weaker job growth and potentially pushing up unemployment . 

 " It 's like a Catch-22 for the Fed , " Alpert says . 

 What the Fed decides to do could be critical for the future of the U.S. economy . If the central bank missteps , it could lead to an inflationary spiral that could be [[hard]] to contain .  Succesvolle werknemers geven organisaties een concurrentievoordeel

 1 . Stop de productiviteitsparanoia 

 De intensiteit van werk is voor veel mensen toegenomen , terwijl managers en HR , toch al bezorgd door signalen van macro - economische achteruitgang , zich niet zelden afvragen of hun werknemers wel productief zijn .

Discussions at the U.N. Climate Change Conference — known as COP27 — are entering the final stretch , with [[just]] days left to thrash out a global climate change deal that both sides can agree upon . 

 But as the conference enters its final days , a draft agreement has been slammed by climate groups who argue it could pave the way to " climate hell . " 

 The COP27 talks have been held over the past two weeks in Glasgow , Scotland , with the aim of formulating a deal that all nations can accept . 

 The current draft agreement , outlined this week , is being criticized by environmental groups and activists . They argue that the current framework focuses too much on individual nations and not enough on the need for collective action to address the global climate emergency . 

 The agreement also does n't set out any clear targets for reducing carbon emissions or a timeline for how those goals should be met , the groups said . 

 " The draft negotiating text is completely inadequate , " said Alden Meyer , the strategic director of the U.S.-based Union of Concerned Scientists . 

 " It does n’t provide an adequate roadmap for how countries will actually meet the commitments they made under the Paris Agreement , and it dangerously falls short of addressing the scale and urgency of the climate crisis we face , " he said in a statement . 

 The Paris Agreement , which was adopted in 2015 , requires nations to set their own targets for curbing climate - warming emissions . But the targets outlined by each nation are voluntary and could be adjusted depending on what is politically possible in each nation . 

 As a result , the emissions targets of all countries are far below the reductions needed to keep global temperatures from rising more than 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre - industrial levels — a target that scientists and economists agree is [[necessary]] to stave off the worst of the climate crisis . 

 Environmental groups argue that the current draft agreement does not go far enough to tackle these issues , as well as the need for more rapid action to shift from fossil fuels to cleaner energy sources . 

 " This deal is paving the way to climate hell , " said Kaisa Kosonen , the international climate policy advisor at Greenpeace . " It is a weak deal that would not ensure the Paris Agreement ’s more ambitious targets are met and further delay urgent climate action , " she said . 

 While the exact details of the [[final]] agreement have yet to be determined , some of the issues have already been discussed — including the potential for countries to create a " loss and damage " mechanism to help poorer nations cope with the impacts of climate change . 

 But the groups fear that without an agreement that is [[ambitious]] enough , these efforts will not be enough to avert the worst of the climate crisis . 

 " The leadership we need from governments at this moment is to come forward with concrete commitments and show ambition to keep global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius and reduce emissions faster than we are now , " said Kat Kramer , the global policy manager of the Climate Action Network . 

 " Governments are falling short of doing that , which is why [[civil]] society is walking away from this deal disappointed and concerned , " she said in a statement . 

 Climate change is already having a devastating impact on communities around the world , including rising sea levels , more extreme weather events and a decline in food security . 

 COP27 is seen as a key moment in the fight against climate change , and governments are expected to come up with an agreement that will help the world reach the goals laid out in the Paris Agreement . 

 But with time running out and the draft agreement facing [[strong]] criticism , it remains to be seen if nations can come up with a deal that will address the urgency of the global climate emergency .

Rosalinda Ballesteros La Ciencia de la Felicidad 

 “ Te felicito . Has llegado a este 31 de diciembre de 2023 en un estado de paz y alegría . Alcanzaste los propósitos que te fijaste hace un año , no sin dificultades , pero valió la pena el sacrificio y esfuerzo . Perseveraste en tu esperanza . Te admiro y te quiero . Recuerdo que tu primer reto era grande , … ” 

 Todos los que hacemos planes quisiéramos escuchar o leer palabras similares al cabo de un año o cualquier periodo que nos fijemos . 

 A veces , no es posible alcanzar ciertas metas ; sin embargo , en la mayoría de los casos se debe a la manera en la que encaramos . No ejercemos un control sobre lo que debemos hacer y no tomamos en cuenta los obstáculos más obvios . 

 Lograr tus propósitos de fin de año tiene muchas recompensas para nuestra vida . Nos ayuda a sentirnos con control sobre nuestro futuro , nos da seguridad sobre nuestra capacidad de realizar tareas y propósitos cada vez más difíciles , y nos hace experimentar un estado de plenitud y felicidad . 

 Te voy a dar una sugerencia para ayudarte a obtener eso que deseas para el próximo 2023 , basada en la Teoría de la Esperanza que desarrolló hace dos décadas el psicólogo C. R. Snyder , profesor de la Universidad de Kansas . 

 Un primer paso , es ponerte metas realmente importantes para ti . No tienen que ser enormes , sino realmente significativas . Si de verdad está en ti querer ser millonario y no tienes un peso , o si quieres ser psicólogo , y te falta la prepa , tienes que avanzar conforme a tus circunstancias actuales . 

 Una vez que descubriste o te fijaste dichas metas , tienes que fijar la ruta . En los ejemplos anteriores , ahorrar para tu primer emprendimiento o acabar la prepa en este 2023 podría ser una buena opción . 

 El tercer paso es creer en tu capacidad de lograrlo . 

 Como ya decíamos , muchas veces abandonamos nuestras metas porque no fijamos un método de control . [[Si]] quiero ser psicólogo , primero debo acabar la prepa lo cual lo puedo hacer en uno o dos años , y posteriormente la licenciatura en psicología que toma entre 4 y 5 años . Hay que ir paso a paso . 

 Cualquier objetivo realmente relevante tiene un camino similar . Quiero aprender a nadar , debo inscribirme a un club deportivo que ofrezca clases de natación ; quiero sacarme la lotería , al menos debo comprar el cachito . ¿ No ? 

 Una Carta de Esperanza puede ser de gran utilidad para tus propósitos . 

 Escríbete a ti mismo una carta con mucho cariño . Féchala , en este caso , el 31 de diciembre de 2023 ( u otra fecha que para tu propósito sea importante ) y háblate en ella como si fueras tu mejor amigo , tu hijo o tu madre . 

 En ella te felicitarás por haber obtenido los resultados deseados con un lenguaje que valore lo mejor posible tu esfuerzo ; y describirás a detalle los retos en enfrentaste . 







 ¡ Claro ! , si hoy tienes una meta , sabes bien qué obstáculos se te pueden oponer y debes detallar ( en tiempo pasado ) cómo los superaste y a quién acudiste para obtener ayuda . 

 Es muy importante que en tu Carta de Esperanza describas las razones por las cuales cada una de tus metas o propósitos realmente valen la pena . 

 Cierra tu carta felicitándonte de nuevo y reconociendo tus fortalezas para lograr lo planeado . 

 Si bien el truco de la carta es que fijes la ruta que seguirás y que entiendas que hay obstáculos que debes sortear , también cumple con la finalidad de programar tu cerebro para que no se desanime ante cualquier imprevisto o la magnitud del esfuerzo . 

 Haz tu Carta de Esperanza , es una actividad de interiorización que te va ayudar a ser mejor de lo que ya eres . Te deseo lo mejor en este ejercicio y para todos estos años que vienen .

A new law signed by President Joe Biden on Wednesday will help memorialize the history of the U.S. government 's incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II . 

 The legislation , spearheaded by Rep. Doris Matsui , D - Calif. , and Sen. Brian Schatz , D - Hawaii , would reauthorize funds that help preserve the sites in which tens of thousands of Japanese Americans were detained , including Manzanar in California and Rohwer in Arkansas . 

 “ The internment of Japanese American citizens remains one of the darkest and most shameful periods in our history , ” Schatz said in a statement about the law . “ The stories of so many who unjustly lost their freedom , lost property , and were forcibly uprooted from their homes should be a constant reminder of our duty to uphold the rights of every American . ” 

 The Norman Y. Mineta Japanese American Confinement Education Act was introduced in the House in March 2021 and passed without objection this year before gaining Senate approval . Mineta , a former secretary of transportation who died last May , was the first Asian American to become a Cabinet secretary and had spent two years in an incarceration camp . 

 The act will not only renew funding for the 2006 Japanese American Confinement Sites Program , but also designate $ 10 million for grants to understand the “ use and abuse of power , ” and promote awareness around this dark period in American history . 

 More than 75 years ago , the U.S. government incarcerated 120,000 Japanese Americans in response to xenophobia and the [[wartime]] hysteria that followed the bombing of Pearl Harbor in 1941 . The community had been deemed a national security threat . Decades later , a federal commission tasked with investigating the wartime exclusion found that the government had moved forward with removal and detention despite there being no documented evidence of a threat of espionage or sabotage . 

 The findings served as the basis for the Civil Liberties Act , signed by President Ronald Reagan in 1988 , offering a formal apology for the mass incarceration , following a [[large]] - scale movement by the Japanese American community . It also provided reparations for surviving victims .

 The Federal Trade Commission on Thursday said it is proposing a rule to ban employers from imposing noncompete agreements on workers and to rescind all existing noncompete agreements . 

 The FTC ’s reasoning : Such agreements , which affect millions of rank - and - file employees and independent contractors across industries , in addition to business executives , have suppressed competition , wages and entrepreneurship . 

 “ Research shows that employers ’ use of noncompetes to restrict workers ’ mobility significantly suppresses workers ’ wages — even for those not subject to noncompetes , or subject to noncompetes that are unenforceable under state law , ” said Elizabeth Wilkins , Director of the Office of Policy Planning . “ The proposed rule would ensure that employers ca n’t exploit their outsized bargaining power to limit workers ’ opportunities and stifle competition . ” 

 The proposed rule was cheered by the liberal - leaning Economic Policy Institute . 

 “ Why do we need this rule ? The only source of power nonunionized workers have vis - à - vis their employers is their ability to quit and take a job elsewhere . So , SURPRISE , employers are using noncompete agreements to cut that source of worker power off at [ the ] knees , ” the organization said in a statement . 

 Still , the proposal ’s broad parameters , if finalized , are likely to be challenged in court . 

 “ As written , this could apply to the janitor and the CEO alike , ” said employment attorney Ashley Herd , founder of ManagerMethod.com and a former human resources executive . 

 One thing the proposed rule would n’t do is ban employers from imposing other types of employment restrictions , such as non - disclosure agreements or non - solicitation agreements that ban employees from poaching a company ’s customers when they leave . 

 But even those could get nixed , the FTC said , if “ they are so broad in scope that they function as noncompetes . ” 

 When might an actual ban take effect ? It could take many months , and possibly push into next year . 

 The proposed rule will be open for public comment for 60 days after which the FTC will review the comments and possibly amend the rule before issuing a final version . 

 But given the broad implications of the proposal Herd said she would n’t be surprised if the deliberation process gets extended by at least a few months .

 But that account was angrily dismissed by an influential military blogger and implicitly contradicted by the leader of the self - declared Donetsk People ’s Republic ( DPR ) in eastern Ukraine , pointing to discord in the [[Russian]] command over Moscow ’s response to the attack . 

 The strike took place just after midnight on Sunday , targeting a [[vocational]] school housing Russian conscripts in Makiivka , in the Donetsk region , according to both Ukrainian and pro - Russian accounts . 

 It prompted a rare Russian admission of a high death toll . The Ukrainian military reported even more dramatic figures , initially claiming up to around 400 Russian soldiers were killed . CNN can not independently verify either side ’s reported death toll . In either case , the strike marks one of the deadliest episodes of the conflict for Moscow ’s forces .

 He questioned how the Ministry of Defense could be “ so sure ” that the location of soldiers lodging in a school building could not have been determined using drone surveillance or a local informant . 

 And he again raised suspicions about the official death toll , which was revised upward by Moscow to 89 from 63 , writing that “ their number will still be growing . ”

 ‘ They ’re putting the blame on each other ’

 “ We know , and we know firsthand , what it is to suffer losses , ” Pushilin said on Telegram Wednesday . “ Based on the information I have , I can say with certainty that there were many displays of courage and [[real]] heroism by the guys in this regiment . ”

 Seúl , Corea del Sur ( CNN ) -- Corea del Norte despidió a Pak Jong Chon , el segundo oficial militar más poderoso después del líder Kim Jong Un , informaron medios estatales . 



 Pak , vicepresidente de la Comisión Militar Central del gobernante Partido de los Trabajadores y secretario del Comité Central , fue sustituido por Ri Yong Gil en la reunión anual del comité que se celebró la semana pasada , según informó este domingo la agencia oficial de noticias KCNA . 

 No se proporcionó ninguna razón para el cambio . Pyongyang renueva periódicamente su dirección , y la reunión anual del partido se ha utilizado a menudo para anunciar cambios de personal y decisiones políticas importantes . 

 La televisión estatal mostró a Pak sentado en la primera fila con la cabeza baja durante la reunión , mientras otros miembros levantaban la mano para votar sobre cuestiones de personal . Más tarde se vio su asiento desocupado . 

 Tampoco apareció en las fotos que publicó este lunes la agencia oficial de noticias KCNA de la visita de Kim durante día de Año Nuevo al Palacio del Sol Kumsusan , que alberga los cuerpos de su abuelo y su padre . Esto marca una diferencia respecto a octubre , cuando Pak acompañó a Kim en un viaje al palacio para conmemorar un aniversario del partido . 

 La Comisión Militar Central del partido , presidida por Kim , se considera el órgano de decisión militar más poderoso del país , por encima del Ministerio de Defensa . 

 publicidad 

 La sustitución de Pak ocurre mientras Kim busca desarrollar nuevos misiles balísticos intercontinentales y un mayor arsenal nuclear para contrarrestar a Estados Unidos y Corea del Sur , como parte clave de la estrategia de defensa del país para 2023 . 

 Pak ascendió rápidamente en el escalafón militar , pasando de comandante de artillería de una estrella en 2015 a general de cuatro estrellas en 2020 , atribuyéndose el mérito de haber contribuido al progreso de la tecnología de misiles de corto alcance del país . 

 A finales de 2020 , Pak recibió el ascenso al politburó y obtuvo el título de mariscal , el rango militar más alto dentro del mandato de Kim . Luego , en noviembre pasado , se convirtió en una de las principales voces en contra de los ejercicios militares conjuntos entre Corea del Sur y Estados Unidos . 

 Como la mayoría de los altos mandos militares que sufrieron altibajos repetidamente bajo el mandato de Kim , Pak fue degradado brevemente a mediados de 2021 después de que Kim reprendiera a algunos oficiales por su gestión de la política contra el covid-19 de Corea del Norte , antes de ser ascendido de nuevo meses más tarde . 

 La destitución de Pak se produce a pesar de que Kim alabó principalmente los avances militares en el desarrollo de armas durante la reunión , a diferencia de otras áreas en las que señaló algunas fallas y pidió mejoras . 

 Oh Gyeong - sup , investigador del Instituto Coreano para la Unificación Nacional de Seúl , dijo que el reciente recrudecimiento de la tensión entre las dos Coreas por la intrusión de drones norcoreanos en el Sur podría haber influido . 

 Funcionarios de Seúl dijeron que Corea del Sur envió tres drones a través de la frontera en respuesta a la intrusión , pero no hubo respuesta del Norte , lo que , según Oh , podría significar que no detectó las aeronaves . 

 " Pak podría haber asumido la responsabilidad del fracaso de las operaciones de seguridad " , dijo Oh . 

 Ri , sucesor de Pak , es también un alto mando militar que ocupó puestos clave , como jefe del Estado Mayor del Ejército y ministro de Defensa .

Jan 3 ( Reuters ) - Japan 's " [[anti]] - Russian course " makes peace treaty talks [[impossible]] , Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Rudenko said in comments published by the state TASS news agency on Tuesday . 

 Russia and Japan have not formally ended World War Two hostilities because of their standoff over islands , seized by the Soviet Union at the end of the war , just off Japan 's northernmost island of Hokkaido . 

 The islands are known in Russia as the Kurils and in Japan as the Northern Territories . 

 " It is absolutely obvious that it is impossible to discuss the signing of such a document ( a peace treaty ) with a state that takes openly unfriendly positions and allows itself direct threats against our country , " Rudenko told TASS in an interview . 

 " We are not seeing signs of Tokyo moving away from the anti - Russian course and any attempt to rectify the situation . " 

 Russia withdrew from its talks with Japan in March last year , following Japanese sanctions over Russia 's invasion of Ukraine . Japan reacted angrily to the talks , calling Moscow 's move " unfair " and " completely unacceptable " . 

 Separately , Rudenko also said that Russia supports Beijing 's " One China " policy on the issue of Taiwan , reiterating Moscow 's explicit backing of China over the fate of the island where the defeated Republic of China government fled in 1949 . 

 " Beijing is well aware that the Russian side invariably supports the People 's ' Republic of China on the Taiwan issue , " Rudenko said . " We proceed from the fact that there is only one China , the PRC government is the only legitimate government representing all of China , and Taiwan is an integral part of it . " 

 China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and has ramped up military and political pressure against the island over the past two years . Taipei strongly rejects Beijing 's sovereignty claims . 

 Reporting in Melbourne by Lidia Kelly ; Editing by Stephen Coates and Christopher Cushing

SHANGHAI , Dec 30 ( Reuters ) - [[Chinese]] tech giant Huawei Technologies Co Ltd ( HWT.UL ) estimated on Friday its 2022 revenue remained flat , suggesting that its sales decline due to U.S. sanctions had come to a halt . 

 Despite sales increasing a mere 0.02 % , rotating chairman Eric Xu struck an upbeat tone in the company 's annual New Year 's letter , where he revealed the figure . 

 " U.S. restrictions are now our new normal , and we 're back to business as [[usual]] , " Xu wrote in the letter that was addressed to staff and released to media . 

 Revenue for the year is expected to be 636.9 billion yuan ( $ $ 91.53 billion ) , according to Xu . 

 That represents a tiny increase from 2021 , when revenue hit 636.8 billion yuan , and marked a 30 % year - on - year sales tumble as the U.S. sanctions on the company took effect . 

 Xu 's letter did not mention Huawei 's profitability . The company typically discloses its full annual results in the following year 's first quarter . 

 A person stands by a sign of Huawei during World Artificial Intelligence Conference , following the coronavirus disease ( COVID-19 ) outbreak , in Shanghai , China , September 1 , 2022 . REUTERS / Aly Song 

 Revenue for 2022 still remained well below the company 's record of $ 122 billion in 2019 . At the time the company was at its peak as the top Android smartphone vendor globally . 

 In 2019 , the U.S. Trump administration imposed a trade ban on Huawei , citing [[national]] security concerns , which barred the company from using Alphabet Inc 's ( GOOGL.O ) Android for its new smartphones , among other critical U.S.-origin technologies . 

 The sanctions caused its handset device sales to plummet . It also lost access to [[critical]] components that barred it from designing its line of processors for smartphones under its HiSilicon chip division . 

 The company continues to generate revenue via its networking equipment division , which competes with Nokia ( NOKIA.HE ) and Ericsson ( ERICb . ST ) . It also operates a cloud computing division . 

 The company began investing in the electric vehicle ( EV ) sector as well as green technologies around the time sanctions took effect . 

 " The macro environment may be rife with uncertainty , but what we can be certain about is that digitisation and decarbonisation are the way forward , and they 're where future opportunities lie , " said Xu in the letter . 

 Reporting by Josh Horwitz ; Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman

On the world stage , the political and military situation remains as tense and uncertain as ever in 2023 . To the dismay of many , World War III is still a possibility , whether it ’s between old foes or as a result of a new disagreement . It ’s impossible to predict with any certainty where a potential conflict may start , but there are a few places around the world that could be the spark to ignite a devastating [[global]] war . 

 Kashmir 

 The region of Kashmir , which is claimed by both India and Pakistan , has been the site of conflict since Partition in 1947 . For decades , Pakistan - backed militants have infiltrated Indian - controlled Kashmir , but the situation has recently become more heated following a surge of violence and upsurge of protests . India ’s attempts to crack down on the unrest have led to greater tension between the two nuclear armed countries , and experts worry that it could escalate into a full - blown war . 

 Taiwan Strait 

 The situation in the Taiwan Strait is perhaps the most dangerous flashpoint in the world today . China considers the region as part of its territory , while Taiwan regards itself as an independent nation . Beijing has become increasingly aggressive towards Taipei in recent years , as it seeks to exert its control over the region . This has led to increased tensions with the United States , which has supported Taiwan in the face of China ’s aggression . It ’s difficult to predict how a potential conflict between the two countries could unfold , but one thing is certain : it would have devastating consequences for the region . 

 Korean Peninsula 

 The Korean peninsula has long been a source of tension in the region . North Korea and South Korea remain technically at war , and the US - backed South Korea has accused North Korea of [[numerous]] provocations . The North has conducted missile tests and continues to expand its nuclear weapons program , while the South has beefed up its military presence near the border . Although an all - out war appears unlikely , the situation could easily flare up and spiral out of control . 

 Ukraine 

 The conflict in Ukraine has been raging since 2014 , when Russia annexed Crimea and backed separatist forces in eastern Ukraine . Since then , Russia has continued to support the separatists , while Ukraine has remained determined to regain control of the region . The United States and its European allies have supported Ukraine in the conflict , which has further strained relations with Russia . The situation is still volatile , and there is always the possibility of a full - scale war between Russia and Ukraine . 

 South China Sea 

 The South China Sea has become a theater of tension and conflict in recent years , as China has attempted to expand its presence in the region . China has been engaging in militarization and [[territorial]] expansion , which has angered the US and its regional allies . As a result , US naval vessels have been sent to patrol the region and “ freedom of navigation ” operations have been conducted in the area . The situation could easily lead to a confrontation between the US and China , which could potentially spiral into a global conflict . 

 While there are other potential flashpoints around the world , the five mentioned above are arguably the most likely places for a potential World War III to start . If any of the situations were to escalate , the consequences for the entire world would be dire . It is , therefore , essential that the international community remain vigilant and work to deescalate any tensions before it ’s too late .

Jeremy Renner , star of Marvel 's Avengers franchise , was reportedly helping a stranded driver during a snowplow accident last night . 

 Mayor John Minto confirmed the news this morning after reports that the actor had been seen in the area . 

 “ Mr. Renner was on the scene and gave aid to a stranded driver , ” Minto said during a press conference . “ He was very heroic and we are incredibly thankful . ” 

 The accident happened at approximately 10:30 p.m. [[local]] time in downtown Anchorage , Alaska . 

 According to witnesses , Renner was driving a snow plow when it suddenly flipped over after hitting a large pothole . 

 The actor quickly jumped out of the vehicle and immediately began to assist the driver in the other vehicle , which had become stranded in the middle of the road . 

 “ He ran over to help the other driver , ” said witness Michael Santiago . “ He even removed his coat and gave it to her to keep her [[warm]] . ” 

 The other driver , who has not been publicly identified , was unharmed but shaken up by the accident . 

 Rescue crews arrived soon after the accident and both Renner and the other driver were taken to a local hospital for [[further]] evaluation . 

 Renner was released shortly after and has since returned to his home in Los Angeles . 

 In a statement , Renner thanked the rescue teams and expressed his gratitude to those who had helped him during the accident . 

 “ I would like to thank all of the rescue personnel who responded to the accident , ” he said . “ I am deeply grateful to the citizens who provided assistance and to the local officials who are currently investigating the accident . ” 

 Mayor Minto also thanked Renner for his actions and said he was proud of the actor for putting his safety at risk to help a complete stranger in need . 

 “ Jeremy is a true hero and an example of what it means to be a good neighbor , ” he said . “ His actions remind us that even in the darkest of times , we can still come together and help each other . ” 

 The accident is still under investigation and no charges have been filed . Renner has yet to make a public comment on the incident .

 The U.S. Department of Justice ( DOJ ) is set to seize [[more]] than $ 465 million worth of Robinhood shares allegedly tied to Bankman - Friedberg , a [[notorious]] fraudulent trading company . 

 The DOJ announced the action on Wednesday as part of an effort to crack down on frauds in the stock market , which have been on the rise in recent months . The action comes in response to a complaint filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission ( SEC ) earlier this year , which accused Bankman - Friedberg of engaging in a [[sophisticated]] market manipulation scheme . 

 The DOJ 's move is aimed at disrupting the fraud , as well as at recovering the funds for victims of the fraud . 

 " This money will help to compensate innocent investors who were harmed by the Bankman - Friedberg fraud , " said U.S. Attorney Andrew Lelling , who is leading the DOJ 's investigation into the company . " We have also stepped up our enforcement efforts to make sure that no one profits from fraud and that we send a strong message that law - breaking will not be tolerated in the markets . " 

 According to the DOJ , Bankman - Friedberg operated a multi - million dollar scheme to manipulate the stock market from the early 2000s through late 2020 . The company used a combination of deceptive trading strategies , including high - frequency trading , layering , spoofing , and mark - ups to artificially inflate stock prices , giving investors false signals as to the true value of the securities . 

 The company 's manipulations were especially effective when trading with Robinhood , a popular investing platform that allows individuals to buy and sell stocks without paying fees or commissions . By exploiting Robinhood 's “ instant settlements ” feature , Bankman - Friedberg was able to quickly move the shares they had purchased , generating millions of dollars in profits at the expense of unsuspecting investors . 

 The DOJ 's case against Bankman - Friedberg is part of a larger effort by the agency to crack down on securities fraud . In recent months , the DOJ has taken legal action against other similar [[fraudulent]] traders , including Gabriel Plotkin , owner of Melvin Capital , for his role in a wide - ranging market manipulation scheme . 

 The government has made clear that it will not tolerate the unlawful gaming of the stock market . In the coming months , the DOJ is [[likely]] to take additional steps to ensure that fraudulent traders are held accountable for their misdeeds . 

 The action against Bankman - Friedberg marks the latest in a series of moves by the DOJ to protect investors and restore confidence in the markets . By seizing the $ 465 million worth of Robinhood shares , the agency is sending a clear message that fraud and dishonesty will not be tolerated and that those who break the law will be held accountable .

Japan 's [[foreign]] minister has called for the creation of a " new world order " to counter the rise of authoritarian regimes across the globe . 

 In a speech to Japan 's legislature on Sunday , Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi stressed the importance of [[collective]] action and international cooperation in the face of global challenges , highlighting the need for a new world order that better reflects the values of democracy and [[human]] rights . 

 “ The international community must make efforts to increase the resilience of our democracies and the capacity for self - determination by reaffirming and strengthening the universal values of democracy and human rights , ” said Motegi . 

 “ In order to prevent the international order from being overturned , it is [[important]] for like - minded countries to build a new world order . ” 

 Motegi highlighted the increasing influence of authoritarian regimes in a number of countries , including China , Russia , Turkey and the Philippines , and urged countries around the world to work together to ensure that freedom of expression and individual rights were respected . 

 “ The rise of authoritarianism is threatening democracy and its universal values , such as human rights and rule of law . It is also a source of increasing global instability , ” said Motegi . 

 The Japanese foreign minister also emphasized the need for better coordination among the world ’s major powers in order to tackle international issues , such as the coronavirus pandemic , climate change and global terrorism . 

 “ In the face of the [[severe]] global situation , the need for a cooperative , proactive and open - minded international order that is based on the recognition of the universality of values has become more [[evident]] , ” said Motegi . 

 Motegi ’s remarks come as the new U.S. Biden administration has indicated it will take a more active role in international affairs and the Indo - Pacific region . 

 The [[foreign]] minister said Japan would cooperate with the United States in areas such as climate change and digital technology , as well as work closely with [[other]] countries to ensure peace and stability in the region . 

 “ Japan will contribute to the peace and stability of the region by strengthening the collective security of Japan , the United States and our allies , ” he said . 

 Motegi ’s call for a new world order echoed a similar call by Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2018 , when he said the global order must be " redefined so that it can reflect the will of the people . ” 

 Motegi ’s remarks were also a nod to the new Biden administration ’s focus on multilateralism and international cooperation , as well as its commitment to the Indo - Pacific region . 

 The Biden administration has indicated it will work closely with its allies in the region , including Japan , to promote an open , rules - based order . 

 While the Biden administration has indicated it will take a tougher stance on China , it has also expressed a willingness to work with Beijing on areas of mutual interest . 

 In the face of rising authoritarianism and the growing challenges posed by China , the Biden administration ’s commitment to the Indo - Pacific region and its openness to international cooperation could be key in establishing a new world order .

CNN — 

 India ’s top court on Friday ordered the release of six people convicted of killing the country ’s former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi , 31 years after their imprisonment . 

 The Supreme Court released Nalini Sriharan , the only woman convicted in the case , and five men , according to Anand Landge , the lawyer for the petitioners . 

 They were arrested a few weeks after Gandhi was assassinated in a suicide bomb attack on May 21 , 1991 , in the southern state of Tamil Nadu . 

 The attack was blamed on separatist rebels fighting for a Tamil state in Sri Lanka . Gandhi ’s killing was seen as retaliation for his decision to send [[Indian]] troops into Sri Lanka in 1987 to enforce a peace accord to end the island nation ’s civil war . 

 Over the years , various Tamil Nadu governments have requested the release of those found guilty over the killing . 

 In May , the Supreme Court ordered the release of A. G. Perarivalan , another man convicted in the case . 

 Perarivalan , who was 19 years old at the time of the attack , was accused of buying batteries for the bomb . He was convicted of criminal conspiracy to commit murder , among [[other]] charges . 

 Known as the “ unwilling ” [[prime]] minister who never wanted the job , Gandhi became India ’s youngest leader at the age of 40 after his mother and former prime minister , Indira Gandhi , was shot dead by her bodyguards . 

 But he served [[less]] than a decade , losing the 1989 general election following a corruption scandal , and was assassinated two years later . 

 During his tenure , he signed peace accords with insurgent groups in states where religious tensions were high , and is credited for developing India ’s science and technology sectors , giving him the moniker “ Father of Information and Technology . ”

In 2018 , Sam Bankman - Fried , the founder of crypto investment firm Alameda Research , faced a crisis that nearly cost him his entire empire . According to a report from Bloomberg , Bankman - Fried scrambled to save his business , offering lenders a 20 % return on their investments . 

 At the time , Bankman - Fried had amassed more than $ 2 billion in cryptocurrency investments . Unfortunately , the bear market of 2018 hit the crypto industry hard , wiping out huge amounts of value . Bankman - Fried ’s firm was no exception , and he needed to find a way to restore confidence in his business and get investors to put their money back into his funds . 

 His solution ? Offer his investors a guaranteed 20 % return . 

 According to the report , Bankman - Fried had a major breakthrough in convincing lenders to back his venture . He was able to negotiate the terms for these loans with lenders , including the Goldman Sachs - backed firm Spring Labs , the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz , and the cryptocurrency venture fund Polychain Capital . 

 These lenders were willing to take a chance on Bankman - Fried and his company , despite the fact that they had no guarantee of repayment . In the end , they agreed to a deal where they would get a return of 20 % on their investments , even if the crypto market collapsed . 

 Bankman - Fried was able to negotiate these terms because of his reputation as a “ one man band ” in the [[crypto]] industry . His success in building his crypto empire from scratch , and his reputation as an innovator , gave him the credibility he needed to attract investors . 

 The deals Bankman - Fried secured provided the capital he needed to survive the bear market . With the additional capital , Alameda Research was [[able]] to shift focus from just trading to providing technology to its customers . By the end of 2018 , Bankman - Fried had successfully managed to turn the company into a fully - fledged technology platform . 

 Today , Bankman - Fried ’s firm is one of the most successful cryptocurrency companies in the world . It is a leader in providing technology to customers , managing millions of dollars in digital assets , and making investments in blockchain - based companies . Bankman - Fried ’s success shows the power of risk - taking and innovation in the world of cryptocurrency . 

 When asked about his experience in 2018 , Bankman - Fried said , “ It was a difficult time and I was pushed to the brink . But , I kept faith in the idea that I could turn it around . Ultimately , I succeeded and today Alameda is one of the largest players in the crypto industry . ” 

 The story of Bankman - Fried and Alameda Research is a testament to the power of innovation and risk - taking . His willingness to take on lenders and offer them returns of 20 % – when traditional investors were not willing to take the risk – was instrumental in ensuring the survival of his business . 

 It is clear that Bankman - Fried is an innovator in the cryptocurrency space and his experience serves as an inspiration for other entrepreneurs . His story shows the rewards that can be reaped from taking risks and investing in innovative companies .
