 On Wednesday , House Republicans will hold their first vote of the new session to replace outgoing House Minority Leader Kevin McCarthy with Rep. Liz Cheney . The vote is the latest evidence of a GOP in disarray — something Democrats and White House officials have highlighted in [[recent]] days . 

 Meanwhile , President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris will host a bipartisan event — their first public event of the Biden administration — at the White House , bringing together both parties for a conversation focused on the nation ’s pandemic - driven economic crisis . 

 It ’s a moment that wo n’t be lost on Washington , as the backdrop of the incoming president ’s first event in office is one of a party in chaos . And while the Biden White House will be focused on trying to bridge the partisan divide , the internal squabbles of the GOP wo n’t be easily forgotten . 

 Indeed , the Republican infighting has been a source of fascination and criticism since the start of the Trump era . 

 When Rep. McCarthy announced last week he would not be running for re - election , the move sent shockwaves through the GOP , with plenty of questions about who will replace him — and what it means for the future of the party . 

 Already , the effort to replace McCarthy is proving to be a [[contentious]] one , with Cheney facing a strong challenge from her [[conservative]] critics in the House Freedom Caucus . A defeat for Cheney , who is seen as more [[moderate]] , would be a major blow to the GOP establishment and the type of split - screen moment Democrats are hoping to take advantage of .

Jan 5 ( Reuters ) - A woman who lived at the house where four University of Idaho students were stabbed to death told investigators she was awakened on the night of the murders by the sound of someone crying in one of the victim 's bedrooms - and then watched as a masked man walked past her and out of the house . 

 The harrowing detail was included in a newly unsealed affidavit on Thursday , just before Bryan Kohberger , the 28 - year - old doctoral student charged with the November slayings , made his first court appearance in Moscow , Idaho . 

 The document also said police have linked Kohberger to the murders using DNA , cell phone data and video footage . 

 The woman , one of two roommates who were left unharmed , told authorities she stood in " frozen shock " shortly after 4 a.m. on Nov. 13 as the man , clad in black , passed by her , before she locked herself in her room . 

 Kohberger , who has been working towards a criminal justice PhD degree at Washington State University , about 10 miles ( 16 kilometers ) from the University of Idaho campus in Moscow , faces four counts of first - degree murder and burglary . 

 He wore an orange jump suit in court and answered " yes " to several questions the judge asked regarding whether he understood the charges against him . He did not enter a plea and will be held without bail . 

 A status hearing was scheduled for Jan. 12 . 

 Kohberger was arrested in Pennsylvania last week , where he was visiting his family , and flown to Idaho on Wednesday . 

 Investigators were able to match DNA recovered from a knife sheath left at the scene with DNA taken from trash at the Kohberger family residence , according to the unsealed affidavit , written by Moscow Police Corporal Brett Payne . 

 Video footage captured a white Elantra , similar to a car registered to Kohberger , passing the house three times on the night of the murders before the driver attempted to park , Payne wrote . About 15 minutes later , the car was seen leaving at a " [[high]] rate of speed . " 

 A Washington State University officer identified Kohberger as the owner of a similar car . 

 Tracking data showed Kohberger 's cell phone appeared to leave the WSU campus around 2:45 a.m. on the night of the attack before going dead for around two hours then reappearing south of Moscow and eventually moving towards his campus home , the affidavit said . 

 The period of time when the phone was not detected is " consistent with Kohberger attempting to conceal his location , " the affidavit said . 

 The crime stunned the small college town in northwestern Idaho . The victims - Ethan Chapin , 20 , of Conway , Washington ; Xana Kernodle , 20 , of Avondale , Arizona ; Madison Mogen , 21 , of Coeur d'Alene , Idaho ; and Kaylee Goncalves , 21 , of Rathdrum , Idaho - all suffered multiple stab wounds , according to authorities . Chapin was Kernodle 's boyfriend . 

 Payne did not suggest a motive for the attack or any connection between Kohberger and the victims . 

 In a survey posted on the social media site Reddit , Kohberger asked participants to help " understand how emotions and psychological traits influence decision making when committing a crime , " the affidavit said . 

 Reporting by Joseph Ax in New York and Brendan O'Brien in Chicago ; Editing by David Gregorio and Howard Goller

For many people , the cost of living in Los Angeles is simply too high . It ’s no surprise that people are looking for alternatives to living in an [[expensive]] metropolis like Los Angeles , where the median rent price is over $ 2,400 per month . 

 That ’s why 44 - year - old Amanda King made the move from California to Indiana a few years ago . Her move has drastically changed her financial situation and she says more people should consider a change of scenery . 

 “ Moving here was the best decision I ever made , ” she said . “ I save at least $ 3,210 per month compared to what I was paying in LA . ” 

 Amanda 's savings are a result of her move from California 's expensive housing market to a more affordable Midwest city . Indiana has no state income tax and its cost of living is almost 10 % lower than the national average . 

 In Los Angeles , Amanda 's monthly rent was $ 2,400 for a one - bedroom apartment . In Indiana , she pays just $ 700 for a two - bedroom condo . The move allowed her to drastically reduce her expenses and ultimately save a substantial amount of money . 

 “ I 'm so much more financially stable here , ” she said . “ In LA , it was always difficult to save and feel like I was getting ahead . But here , I actually feel like I 'm building a future . ” 

 In addition to her rental savings , Amanda says she has also reduced her food , entertainment , and transportation costs . She rarely goes out to eat , instead opting to shop at farmer ’s markets and grocery stores . She also uses public transportation more , taking advantage of the affordable bus and train systems . 

 Amanda says she spends her free time exploring the city and attending local events . She has found that Indiana has a lot to offer , from great art and culture to outdoor activities like hiking and fishing . 

 “ There ’s still plenty to do here , ” she said . “ You just have to look for it and be willing to take a chance . ” 

 Amanda also credits her move to Indiana for her overall improved quality of life . She says she is much less stressed here and enjoys living a much simpler life . 

 “ LA is the glitz and glamour , but when you take that aside , are you really living the life that you want to live ? ” she said . “ For me , living in the Midwest was a breath of [[fresh]] air . ” 

 For anyone looking to make a similar move , Amanda says the key is to do plenty of research . She recommends looking into the different cities , understanding their economies , and finding the places that suit you best . 

 “ If you ’re willing to open your mind and give it a shot , there are so many great places to live that do n’t require you to be a millionaire , ” she said . 

 Amanda hopes that by telling her story , more people will be inspired to make the move and experience the quality of life she ’s been able to achieve . She says that while it was n’t always easy , she does n’t regret her decision to move .

Dania Akeel became the first female competitor from Saudi Arabia to tackle the world ’s toughest motor race , the Dakar Rally , when she recently took part in the 2021 edition . 

 The 34 - year - old ’s achievement was all the more impressive as it came just three years after she first touched a motorbike . 

 “ I was n’t into cars or bikes , but then one day my friends invited me to the desert to ride a quad bike , and I just loved it ! ” Akeel told CNN Sport . “ I had no idea I was going to go on to do something like this . ” 

 Akeel , who hails from the port city of Jeddah , where she works as a lawyer , was first introduced to motor racing in 2018 . Her interest in the sport only grew from there , and soon she was taking part in off - road events in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates . 

 Encouraged by her success in the region , Akeel decided to take on the Dakar Rally in 2021 . It was a huge undertaking , given the difficulty of the event — made up of long stages and arduous terrain — and the fact that no Saudi woman had ever entered before . 

 “ I thought , why not me ? I knew that it was going to be very hard and [[challenging]] , but I wanted to be the first [ Saudi ] girl who tried , ” she said . 

 Akeel received support from the Saudi Arabian Motor Federation , who sponsored her participation and provided her with a team and a bike . She then set to work preparing for the toughest race in the world , putting in long hours at the gym and practicing on both the sand dunes and motocross tracks . 

 The experience , however , was a [[steep]] learning curve . 

 “ The weather and the terrain were so different from what I was used to in Saudi , ” said Akeel . “ The Dakar Rally has been running for over 40 years , so the more experienced riders have a lot of knowledge and know what to expect . For me , it was a whole new world . ” 

 Despite the challenges she faced , Akeel managed to complete the 5,518 - mile ( 8,890 km ) race , crossing the finish line in Jeddah in April after 16 days of gruelling desert driving . 

 Not only was she the first female from Saudi Arabia to have taken part , but she also became the first female in the Arab world to have completed the full race . 

 “ It was so amazing to finish , and even more so to be able to share this achievement with people back home , ” Akeel said . “ I hope that my experience can encourage other women and girls to go for their dreams , no matter how ambitious they might seem . ” 

 Akeel ’s success has been celebrated widely in the region and beyond , with her story appearing on the news and in newspapers across the Middle East . And it has certainly not been lost on the racing world , either . 

 Indeed , Akeel has been invited to take part in a range of international rallies and events , such as the Dakar Series and the World Rally Championship . 

 “ It ’s so humbling and gratifying to see that what I ’ve achieved has had such a positive impact , ” she said . “ It ’s a huge honor to be invited to participate in these events . I know it wo n’t be easy , but I ’m up for the challenge . ” 

 For now , Akeel is determined to make the most of her newfound fame and use it to inspire more Saudi women to try their hand at motor racing . 

 “ I want to encourage Saudi women to go out and follow their passions , ” she said . “ I hope to show them that anything is possible . ” 

 It has certainly been a journey that Akeel would never have expected when she first set foot on a motorbike . But one that has been made all the more remarkable by the fact that she achieved it alone — without a team or any sponsorship — and inspired so many other women along the way . 

 It is a feat that is worthy of its own Dakar Rally . And for Dania Akeel , it is only the start .

 House Minority Leader Kevin McCarthy is struggling to corral the Republican votes necessary to become the next House speaker , even as he maintains an iron grip on the race . 

 In a matter of days , a [[potential]] once - in - a - century fight is set to unfold on the House floor as McCarthy , a close ally of President Donald Trump , and House Majority Leader Steny Hoyer , the No . 2 House Democrat , vie for the top spot . 

 The speaker 's election will require a majority of the House and its 435 members , meaning McCarthy and Hoyer must capture 218 votes apiece . Republicans control the House , but some members , including those from the hard - line Freedom Caucus , have been withholding their support from McCarthy . 

 If neither McCarthy nor Hoyer can secure the votes , a " wildcard " speaker may emerge , potentially the current House Minority Whip , Steve Scalise , who is the only House Republican to publicly confirm his desire to be speaker . 

 A [[third]] - party candidate could also enter the fray . A senior Republican source close to the speaker 's race told CNN , " I think we need to be prepared that anything can happen . " 

 The scene is a dramatic one , and the stakes could not be higher . 

 At a press conference on Wednesday , McCarthy , who has served as House minority leader since 2014 , was guarded in his remarks . 

 He tried to cast a positive light on the situation but did not directly address the fact that he has yet to secure the necessary Republican votes . 

 " We are in discussions and we are [[excited]] about the upcoming challenge of taking the House majority , " McCarthy said . " We have the plan , we have the strategy and I 'm confident that our team and our ideas will prevail . " 

 But as of Thursday , McCarthy was still several votes short of the 218 needed to win , and the math has been complicated by divisions among Republicans about the direction of their party .

Separar los mitos de los hechos sobre lavarse la cara puede ser confuso . 

 Los dermatólogos recomiendan usar un limpiador que se adapte bien a tu tipo de piel , en lugar de una barra de jabón . 

 Lavarse la cara dos veces al día no siempre es necesario , pero lavarla una vez puede prevenir los brotes . 

 ¿ Ya conoces nuestra cuenta en Instagram ? Síguenos . 

 1 . “ No hay que lavarse la cara en la regadera ” 

 Aunque algunos piensan que lavarse la cara no debe ser parte de su rutina de baño en la regadera , puede ser algo bueno siempre que tengas cuidado , dijo Shasa Hu , dermatóloga certificada y cofundadora del servicio de consulta de cuidado de la piel BiaLife . 

 “ Cuando te lavas la cara en la regadera , el rocío tibio de promueve una exfoliación más profunda y destapa los poros ” , explicó Hu . 

 “ Mientras no uses agua muy caliente o jabones fuertes , lavarte la cara mientras te bañas te ahorrará tiempo , ahorrará agua y te brindará una limpieza más profunda para preparar tu piel para el resto de tu rutina de cuidado de la piel ” , agregó . 

 2 . “ Siempre debe lavarse la cara dos veces al día ” 

 La dermatóloga con sede en la ciudad de Nueva York , Hadley King , dijo a Insider que lavarte la cara dos veces al día depende de tu tipo de piel y de lo que necesites . 

 Los tipos de piel seca o sensible están bien para limpiarse una vez por la noche , pero la piel grasa puede requerir que la limpies al menos dos veces al día . 

 Pero si haces una actividad física que te hace sudar mucho o usas mucho maquillaje , ella recomendó que te laves la cara después del gimnasio o antes de dormir . 

 “ La limpieza antes de dormir generalmente se recomienda no [[solo]] para eliminar el maquillaje , sino también la suciedad y la contaminación que se acumula en nuestra piel durante el día ” , dijo . 

 Esas partículas pueden causar daño oxidativo y contribuir a la descomposición del colágeno y las arrugas . 

 “ Si usa productos para la piel durante la noche que dejan un residuo o una capa en la piel , es probable que también desee limpiarte la cara por la mañana ” , añadió . 

 3 . “ Tus productos solo son efectivos si tu cara siente una ligera quemadura o estirada después de su uso ” 

 “ Sin dolor , no hay ganancia ” no se aplica cuando se trata del cuidado de la piel , dijo Audrey Kunin , dermatóloga y fundadora de la marca clínica de cuidado de la piel DERMAdoctor . 

 “ Cuando la piel se quema o irrita con los ingredientes para el cuidado , altera el manto ácido protector de la piel , lo que puede producir una mayor sensibilidad de la piel e incluso a una infección ” , explicó . 

 Pero ciertos ácidos y retinoides fuertes recetados pueden producir una ligera sensación de ardor o una reacción de descamación hasta que la piel se haya adaptado , de acuerdo con Hu . 







 “ En general , estos síntomas desaparecen a medida que el ingrediente activo vuelve a equilibrar la renovación celular ” , añadió Hu . 

 Si no estás seguro de si la reacción de tu piel a un producto es normal o no , comunícate con un dermatólogo antes de continuar usándolo . 

 4 . “ Lavarse la cara con agua y jabón es suficiente ” 

 “ El jabón normal es para limpiar cosas normales . Tu piel no es normal ” , afirmó a Insider Rachel Nazarian , dermatóloga de la ciudad de Nueva York . 

 Los jabones convencionales eliminarán tus aceites naturales , “ interrumpirán el pH de tu piel y dañarán la barrera ” , dijo , lo que puede causar sequedad e irritación . 

 En su lugar , lávate la piel con un limpiador suave y sin fragancia que ofrezca una limpieza profunda y se adapte a tu complexión única . 

 5 . “ Frotar con un cepillo de limpieza es la mejor manera de obtener una limpieza profunda ” 

 Contrariamente a la creencia popular , frotar con una toallita o dispositivos mecánicos no eliminará el aceite o los polímeros del maquillaje de la superficie de la piel , de acuerdo con Hu . 

 “ Con el tiempo , tu piel responde a la exfoliación mecánica agresiva produciendo más aceite , lo que puede provocar obstrucciones ” , dijo a Insider . “ Esto a menudo se convierte en un círculo vicioso ” . 

 Los limpiadores mecánicos pueden incluso causar “ fisuras microscópicas ” en la piel que pueden aumentar el riesgo de una reacción alérgica o irritación de la piel . 

 Si debes frotar , usa un paño de muselina suave o un limpiador exfoliante suave . 

 6 . “ Tienes acné porque no te lavas la cara todos los días ” 

 Aunque mantener una tez limpia definitivamente ayuda a prevenir los brotes , existen otros factores , como la genética y las hormonas , que pueden causar acné , de acuerdo con King . 

 “ Si tienes la piel grasa y eres propensa al acné , entonces sí , es posible que tengas más poros obstruidos y brotes de acné si no te lavas la cara con regularidad ” , dijo . “ Pero si no eres particularmente grasoso o propenso al acné , no es tan probable que no te laves la cara todos los días ” . 

 7 . “ No debes usar una toallita para secarte la cara ” 

 Secarse la cara con una toallita solo puede ser realmente problemático en dos situaciones : primero , si la toallita está contaminada con bacterias , levaduras u hongos , y segundo , si la toallita es tan abrasiva que provoca irritación . 

 King dijo que por lo general está bien usar un paño limpio en la cara si “ se seca suavemente sin frotar ” . 

 8 . “ No es necesario que te quites el maquillaje antes de lavarte la cara ” 

 Algunas personas creen que un limpiador puede quitar el maquillaje y limpiar la piel de una sola vez . No obstante , Hu recomendó que la eliminación del maquillaje sea el primer paso de tu rutina de cuidado de la piel . 

 “ El maquillaje tiene pigmentos , conservadores , minerales y metales que a menudo [[pueden]] obstruir los poros si se dejan demasiado tiempo … e impiden la penetración de los productos para el cuidado de la piel ” , [[explicó]] . “ Es fundamental desmaquillarse como primer paso en tu rutina de noche ” . 

 9 . “ Lavarse la cara con solo una toallita desmaquilladora es suficiente ” 

 Aunque desmaquillarse debería ser el primer paso de tu rutina nocturna , no debería ser el único paso , de acuerdo con Nazarian , especialmente si usas toallitas desmaquillantes . 

 “ Las toallitas limpiadoras eliminan la mayor parte de las bacterias , la suciedad y el aceite , pero también dejan un rastro de residuos ” , dijo . « Esto puede provocar potencialmente acné e infección de glándulas , especialmente alrededor de los párpados y las pestañas . La limpieza facial adecuada requiere un enjuague a base de agua para limpiar completamente ” . 

 10 . “ No tienes que lavarte las manos antes de lavarte la cara ” 

 Incluso si tus manos no se ven ni se sienten sucias , siempre es mejor lavarlas antes de tocarse la cara , explicó Hu . 

 “ La mayoría de las personas usan las manos con frecuencia para escribir en teclados y teléfonos , o para manejar ” , dijo . 

 Las bacterias y los productos químicos en estas superficies pueden provocar irritación o infección en la piel y los ojos , especialmente en personas propensas al eccema .

The album cover was one of my [[first]] photoshoots . I was so excited , but also had no idea what to expect . We started early . Getting ready for the shoot was just me using what I had with me . We were originally shooting inside , but my gut told me to walk outside and explore what the city had to offer . Here are eight of those books that I recommend to anyone looking for a little self - improvement : 

 1 . The 7 Habits of Highly [[Effective]] People by Stephen R. Covey 

 The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People is one of the all - time best - selling self - help books . This classic work examines seven core principles to help readers become more efficient and effective in their lives . Covey dives deep into each of the habits and provides step - by - step guidance on how to make them a part of your daily life . 

 2 . The Power of Now by Eckhart Tolle 

 The Power of Now , written by spiritual teacher Eckhart Tolle , is a modern [[spiritual]] classic . It encourages readers to live in the moment and be [[mindful]] of their thoughts , feelings , and actions . It ’s a powerful exploration of the present moment and how to use it as a source of strength and growth . 

 3 . How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie

 4 . Emotional Intelligence by Daniel Goleman 

 Emotional Intelligence is an important book for anyone who wants to better understand themselves and those around them . It examines the power of emotions and how to use them as a tool for achieving success in relationships and in life . 

 5 . Man ’s Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl 

 Man ’s Search for Meaning , written by psychiatrist Viktor E. Frankl , is an inspiring exploration of the human spirit in the face of adversity . It chronicles Frankl ’s experience in a Nazi concentration camp and his journey to find meaning in a seemingly meaningless existence . 

 6 . The Art of Possibility by Rosamund Stone Zander and Benjamin Zander

 7 . The Power of Positive Thinking by Norman Vincent Peale 

 The Power of Positive Thinking is a classic self - help book that teaches readers how to develop a more optimistic outlook on life . It explores the power of positive thinking and how it can help readers to achieve their goals and live a happier life . 

 8 . You Are a Badass by Jen Sincero 

 You Are a Badass is an inspiring and humorous book for anyone looking for a little boost . It offers encouragement , laughs , and plenty of life lessons on how to overcome fear and create a life you love . 

 While there are hundreds of self - help books out there , the eight books listed above are some of the best . I hope that these titles will provide you with the guidance and insight needed to embark on a journey of personal growth and self - discovery .

 Those are the words of Hope Hicks , one of Donald Trump ’s most loyal aides , in a text she sent to Ivanka Trump ’s chief of staff on January 6 , 2021 . They are a fitting epitaph for the Trump presidency . 

 Two years ago today , a pro - Trump mob stormed the U.S. Capitol to stop the certification of the 2020 presidential election . Seven people died as a result of that attempt . More than 140 police officers reported suffering injuries . One was pulled down the steps of the Capitol and then stomped on and beaten with a pole flying an American flag as the crowd chanted “ U.S.A. ! U.S.A. ! ” A makeshift gallows with a noose was built outside the Capitol , not as a generalized threat but to cow one man . “ Hang Mike Pence ! ” the mob shouted . If the insurrectionists had had the opportunity , they would have . Most stunning of all , the president of the United States encouraged the bloodlust .  Peter Wehner : The Trump abandonment has begun 

 The many millions who watched the events unfold instantly knew that it would rank among the most anguished and horrifying days in American history : an effort to halt the peaceful transition of power . But it was worse and more wretched than we imagined . 

 We know this thanks to the [[extraordinary]] work of the House Select Committee that investigated the January 6 attacks . The bipartisan committee , which over the course of an 18 - month inquiry held 10 [[public]] hearings , released a more - than-800 - page report on December 22 . It was the result of more than 1,200 witness interviews and a review of more than 1 million pages of documents that were obtained because of the issuance of more than 100 subpoenas . Americans learned the details of a deliberate , [[coordinated]] , violent , multipart plan to overturn the 2020 [[presidential]] election . And the main actor was the nation ’s president . 

 “ The central cause of January 6 was one man , former President Donald Trump , whom many others followed , ” the report said . “ None of the events of January 6 would have happened without him . ” 

 Trump knew that his claims to have won the election were lies . That did n’t matter . He and his allies pressured state officials , high - ranking functionaries in the Department of Justice , and his own vice president to join him in his effort . They created a fake - elector plan . They invented [[legal]] theories to justify a coup . They tried to block certification of the election . But their endeavors did n’t stop there . Trump “ lit the flame ” that ignited the January 6 mob , in the words of [[former]] Representative Liz Cheney . 

 As the mayhem was ramping up on January 6 , a colleague texted Hope Hicks , “ Hey , I know you ’re seeing this . But he really should tweet something about Being NON - violent . ” To which Hicks replied , “ I ’m not there . I suggested it several times Monday and Tuesday and he refused . ” The White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson testified that , as aides and family were begging the president to take steps to stop the violence , she overheard Chief of Staff Mark Meadows telling White House Counsel Pat Cipollone , “ He does n’t want to do anything , Pat . ” And in a text sent on the afternoon of January 6 , when the violence was reaching an apex , Trump ’s aide Robert Gabriel wrote , “ Potus i m sure is loving this . ” 

 Frantic and deranged , Trump made every possible effort to upend [[American]] democracy . The violence , the bloodshed , was for him an added bonus . 

 The power of the Select Committee report — eight chapters , four appendices , thousands of footnotes — is not its eloquent language ; it is its clarity and coherence ; the firsthand testimonies , contemporaneous evidence , and stunning , intricate details ; and its skill at narrating a story that , in the pre [[-]] Trump era , would have seemed not just improbable but surreal , even mad .

Hutchinson testified that just minutes before addressing the crowd , President Trump shouted to his advance team : ‘ I do n’t [ fucking ] care that they have weapons . They ’re not here to hurt me . Take the [ fucking ] mags away . Let my people in . They can march to the Capitol from here . Take the [ fucking ] mags away . ’ ”

The committee accused Trump of obstructing an official proceeding , conspiracy to defraud the United States , making knowingly and willfully materially false statements to the federal government , and inciting or assisting an insurrection . 

 The Select Committee ’s report focuses on the protagonist in this malefic drama . That is understandable ; Trump , after all , was the indispensable man in everything that unfolded . But not [[enough]] attention has been focused on the Republican Party , which was institutionally indispensable to what happened on January 6 . 

 I say that not only because Trump was the leader of the Republican Party when he engineered the insurrection but because the GOP stood with Trump at every moment in his corrupt and corrupting presidency . Republicans defended him , supported him , empowered him , deflected attention away from him , and made excuses for him . For that reason , they are partly responsible for the insurrection .

That was expected , I suppose , because during the Trump era , the GOP was a battering ram against truth and reality .

 Ford said it sold more than 75,000 F - Series pickups in December , a 20.1 % increase compared with a year earlier and the best month of the year as parts and supply chain problems disrupted production . Sales of the trucks still ended the year down 9.9 % but better than the 13 % they were down through November . 

 Andrew Frick , Ford vice president of sales , distribution & trucks , said the company is " well positioned heading into 2023 . " However , the automaker did not release a sales forecast for the year . 

 Ford 's 2022 sales outpaced the industry , which was estimated to be down by roughly 9 % . But they were not able to match crosstown rival General Motors , which managed to eke out a 2.5 % gain in sales compared with 2021 . 

 Ford said it was able to gain 0.7 percentage points of market share in 2022 , but that was n't enough to offset its 1.3 percentage point loss from the prior year . 

 Regarding all - electric vehicles , Ford said it was able to maintain its status as the country 's second - best seller of EVs . Despite more than doubling its EV sales , Ford trails industry leader Tesla by a [[wide]] margin .

Author Susan Kuklin : These teens wanted to let [[other]] kids know ' they are not [[alone]] ' 

 Enlarge this image toggle caption Kaz Fantone / NPR Kaz Fantone / NPR 

 This essay by Susan Kuklin is part of a series of interviews with — and essays by — authors who are finding their books being challenged and banned in the U.S. 

 In 2014 , when my book Beyond Magenta : Transgender Teens Speak Out was published , little had been written or said publicly about transgender and nonbinary teens . 

 Beyond Magenta centers around six young adults , members of the trans / nonbinary community , who describe their struggles and their triumphs , their feelings and experiences when dealing with their personal identities . They speak of themselves and their community simply , introspectively — and with gravity , warmth and humor . 

 I was [[surprised]] when the book appeared on the American Library Association ( ALA ) list of challenged books in 2015 : I had been interviewing and photographing young adults for years , covering contemporary topics such as teen pregnancy , suicide , AIDS , prejudice , human rights , teens on death row , and immigration but — as far as I know — none of those books had been banned from library bookshelves or classrooms . My reasoning , evidently naïve , was that because these accounts were written from the point of view of people directly experiencing said issues ( based on my extensive interviews with them ) , readers would respect the participants ' right to self - expression and that they would appreciate the informative value of their candor . 

 All six participants in Beyond Magenta chose to speak to me for three primary reasons : They wanted to define themselves publicly in their own terms ; they wanted to educate others ; and they wanted to let other young people in similar situations know that they are not alone . My own reasoning for covering them was all of the above — along with the belief that once a person gets to meet and learn about someone from a group they might not otherwise know , they will be more open to them . 

 Who are these young people ? Jessie , a trans man , is so comfortable in his skin he makes everyone else share the joy of his transition . Christina , a trans woman , attended a parochial boys ' high school in the Bronx . Mariah was born into a disadvantaged , violent family and grew up in institutions . Cameron , who lives with a supportive family , deftly explains that " gender is more fluid and more complex than society assumes . " Nat describes themself as intersex , both male and female , neither male nor female . And lastly there 's Luke , who writes poetry to tell his story . 

 When the book first came out it received [[many]] positive , starred reviews , including including in publications for librarians and educators like Publishers Weekly and Kirkus . [[Young]] people and quite a few parents wrote thanking me for publishing it . And some things happened that I had not experienced with my previous books : During school and library visits , one or two teens would often hang back from their next class to talk privately . The discussion was always the same : I need to read your book , but my parents wo n't let me . It was heartbreaking . Six people sent emails that they were on the verge of suicide . One high school student in a rural , conservative town wrote that they were so lonely and desperate they had been planning their death for that very day . But passing a bookstore on the way home , they saw the person on the cover of Beyond Magenta who looked exactly like them . Flipping through the pages of the book , they found a first name in it that was their name too . It was a sign — they were not alone . I still get goosebumps thinking of that teen and hope they live a long , happy life . Those six emails alone are [[worth]] what followed next . 

 It was a Saturday night a few years ago and I was lying on the couch reading on my iPad . Suddenly , a vulgar tweet about me popped up . It complained about a paragraph in Beyond Magenta , one that I did n't even remember . Then another tweet . And another . And another . Suddenly there were hundreds of them . " I think I have a virus on the iPad , " I told my husband . " Turn it off now , " he said , and I did . The following Monday morning my editor called to tell me that our book had gone viral — that it was being challenged . 

 It felt otherworldly . Creepy . Wrong . Then , with elections approaching , some cynical and cruel politicians jumped on the anti [[-]] trans bandwagon to stir up voters . They vilified trans children , their parents , the LGBTQ+ community and their literature . 

 I became more than a little worried . Although the identities of the participants were well - hidden and protected , I worried about their reactions . They had worked so hard to find and express their true selves , surely they did n't need this . As the author , it was disappointing that my intention of bringing together contributors and readers was reinterpreted — misinterpreted — by paragraphs taken out of context , mostly by people who , it became apparent , had not even read the book . I worried that future publishers might stop publishing so - called controversial books and that writers would be less ready to write them . ( That did n't happen . ) I was also concerned that librarians and teachers could suffer , even lose their jobs , for doing what they trained to do — teach . 

 My publisher continues to guide and support me though this odyssey of animosity and suppression . They still publish my books . It helps that friends and colleagues have my back , as does PEN America and its Children 's Young Adult Book Committee . The American Library Association , The National Committee Against Censorship , and American Civil Liberties Union stand by writers whose books have been challenged . And many parents and students face hostile school board meetings to protect their right to choose what books they have access to at school . I 'm so proud of everyone associated with Beyond Magenta , especially the brave , young people interviewed . 

 If you are a young person thinking about harming yourself , you can contact a counselor at the Trevor Project at any time via private call text , or chat : https://www.thetrevorproject.org/get-help/ 

 Susan Kuklin is a photographer and author of nonfiction books , many for children and young adults . Find her at her website here .

In recent years , a new concept has been gaining traction in political and economic circles : degrowth . Degrowth is an idea put forward by scholars and activists , suggesting that societies and economies can achieve sustainability by reducing their consumption and production of goods and services . While some view the concept as a utopian pipe dream , others are beginning to take it seriously , pointing to degrowth as the only viable solution to the world 's biggest problems . 

 At its core , degrowth is an economic system built on the understanding that the world 's resources are finite . It proposes that societies should reduce their levels of consumption and production in order to bring the environment back into balance . In other words , it 's a model of economic development that puts the planet first . 

 Proponents of degrowth argue that it is the only way to combat climate change , reduce inequality , and build a more equitable society . They suggest that a degrowth - based economy would be more decentralized and democratic , with a focus on local and regional production and consumption . It would also promote a different relationship between people and the environment . 

 But , critics say that degrowth is unrealistic and dangerous . They point to its potential for economic stagnation , as well as its likely impact on global trade and the global economy . They argue that degrowth could lead to job losses , rising inequality , and a new set of economic problems . 

 However , supporters of degrowth counter these arguments by noting that the current economic system is already unsustainable , and it ’s only a matter of time before it implodes . In addition , they point to recent successes in countries such as Norway , where degrowth measures have been implemented . 

 In Norway , the government has imposed a maximum limit on public spending , with the goal of achieving greater economic stability and sustainability . This approach has allowed the country to reduce its emissions and improve its energy efficiency , while also ensuring that public services and programs are adequately funded . As a result , Norway has become a leader in environmental protection and renewable energy , and its economy has grown steadily over the past few years . 

 While Norway ’s experience is certainly encouraging , the concept of degrowth still faces [[significant]] hurdles before it can become the norm . For one , the idea is still largely seen as radical , and many people are wary of its [[potential]] impacts on the global economy . 

 At the same time , some suggest that degrowth is the only real solution to the world ’s [[biggest]] problems , and that the world needs to embrace it in order to avoid a [[catastrophic]] collapse . As [[renowned]] economist Kate Raworth put it , “ we need to ditch growth or else face disastrous climate change , escalating inequality and collapsing ecosystems . ” 

 Ultimately , whether or not degrowth is the right approach is a matter of debate . But one thing is certain : it is an idea that is gaining traction , and one that needs to be taken seriously . It is clear that the world needs a new approach to economic development , one that puts sustainability and equity first . If we are to avert a [[potential]] disaster , then degrowth is an idea that we can no longer ignore .

Stocks usually go up . Just make sure to give it 20 years : Morning Brief 

 This article first appeared in the Morning Brief . Get the Morning Brief sent directly to your inbox every Monday to Friday by 6:30 a.m. ET . Subscribe 

 Tuesday , January 3 , 2022 

 Today 's newsletter is by Myles Udland , senior markets editor at Yahoo Finance . Follow him on Twitter @MylesUdland and on LinkedIn . Read this and more market news on the go with the Yahoo Finance App . 

 After a brutal 2022 , investors are thrilled to see the calendar flip over to 2023 . 

 The S&P 500 suffered its worst year since the [[financial]] crisis in 2008 . By one measure , the bond market had its [[worst]] year on record . 

 And while some investors are still licking wounds from one of the most challenging years in a generation , others may see a market full of opportunities to buy great companies at big discounts . 

 As the investment world spends the next few months — or more — figuring out just what went [[wrong]] in 2022 , there 's little doubt we 'll hear reminders about the positive long - term track record of the stock market . 

 And why would n't we ? 

 As one of our favorite charts from JPMorgan Asset Management shows , stocks usually go up : Since 1980 , the S&P 500 has been positive in 32 of 43 years . 

 About 75 % of the time since 1980 , the S&P 500 has gone up . Cold comfort , perhaps , after investors just endured the worst year for stocks since 2008 . ( Source : JPMorgan Asset Management ) 

 Now , after a year that saw conservative investment portfolios like the 60/40 mix of stocks and bonds lose [[more]] than 15 % , it 's little comfort telling a client years like this are outside the norm . 

 And when making references to history showing time is on the side of the patient investor , you 've got to be sure to choose the right timeframe to back up the case for buying stocks for the long run . 

 And the " right " timeframe is 20 years . 

 In a note to clients published [[last]] week , Nicholas Colas , cofounder of DataTrek Research , flagged the historical record for the S&P 500 's rolling compounded annual growth , which shows the benchmark index returns an average of 10.8 % per year , or 7.1 % annually when adjusted for inflation . 

 And over that stretch , stocks have never been negative over a 20 - year period . 

 Story continues 

 Over any 20 - year rolling period since 1947 , U.S. stocks have been higher . Though not all historical periods are created equal . Not by a long shot . ( Source : DataTrek Research ) 

 Again , stocks usually go up . 

 " History shows that 20 years of continuous investment is the bare minimum to be assured of a [[positive]] real return for the S&P 500 , " Colas wrote . " One can do very well over a [[shorter]] period if all the stars are aligned , of course . But … two decades is the ' right ' long term timeframe to use in a mental model of how long it can take for US equities to generate value for investors . " 

 Of course , not all 20 - year periods are created equal . 

 For periods ended in 1961 and 1999 — which capped the post - World War II boom and the post - Volcker inflation crush , respectively — the S&P 500 showered investors with annualized returns of 13.3 % and 13.7 % , respectively , after adjusting for inflation . 

 Nice work if you can get it . 

 On the flip side , the deleterious effects of inflation that plagued the economy in the ' 70s and ' 80s — as well as the aftermath of the tech bust that began in 1999 — saw 20 - year average annual returns after the impact of inflation fall to a mere 0.9 % and 3.4 % , respectively , for periods ending in 1982 and 2018 . 

 Eagle - eyed readers will also notice these good and bad periods follow one after the [[other]] . In markets , as in life , there 's a time to reap and a time to sow . 

 Another conundrum Colas ' work shows investors facing today is how to proceed after a year that punished equity investors — but one that appears to fit within an improving long - term trend for patient investors . 

 " Stock returns drive asset allocation , " Colas wrote . " Ever wonder why we 've seen a veritable explosion of interest in venture and private equity over the last 10 - 12 years , or several virtual currency bubbles in the same timeframe ? " 

 Institutional investors today are looking at equity allocations , which have underperformed that average annual return of 10.8 % and 7.1 % before and after inflation , and are looking for alternatives . No wonder the broad umbrella of private equity , real estate , and venture is literally called " alts . " 

 But what ultimately drives stock prices higher is earnings . And what drives earnings , in Colas ' view , is " a [[happy]] confluence of [[macro]] factors and coincident booms in consumer spending . " 

 They do n't call them " Baby Boomers " for no reason . And though the tech bubble ultimately overstated the promise for investors , [[steady]] innovation through the ' 80s and ' 90s — along with another demographic surge as Millennials were born — powered the economy . 

 And if there is a continued push higher in average stock returns over the next decade , it will have to be powered by some force , some " happy confluence " of real improvements in the economy . 

 Perhaps some promises of the crypto industry are fulfilled as technological leaps for the consumer economy . 

 Perhaps another demographic boom brought on by Millennials having children powers growth in the years ahead . 

 But whatever the details , the broad outline is clear . As Colas wrote : " Any increase in structural returns now will require the same ingredients , stirred vigorously with human ingenuity unhampered by external forces . "
